articles.title: Planning to go to an Apple Store to pick up an iPhone Duo on Friday? You might be disappointed
articles.text:
'Nothing short of extraordinary': high iPhone Duo demand means you probably won't be able to pick up Apple's foldable by walking into a store on October 23
Apple's foldable is proving popular
- iPhone Duo shipping dates have slipped to January worldwide
- Stock may be limited if you're trying to pick one up in an Apple Store too
- Retail availability and the first preorder shipments due on October 23
We've already had one indication that iPhone Duo sales were going rather well when shipping dates for preorders started slipping into next year, and now Apple is apparently telling retail staff that availability will be limited inside stores too.
According to Apple Store employees speaking to MacRumors, Apple has said that customers without a preorder should be warned against heading to their local outlet in the expectation of picking up an iPhone Duo on Friday, October 23.
That's the designated day when online preorders are due to start shipping out to buyers, and when — in theory — the iPhone Duo becomes available to buy in store. This latest report suggests that might not be possible right away.
It isn't clear if the instructions given to the Apple Store employees speaking to MacRumors apply across the US or globally, but set your expectations accordingly: don't assume you'll be able to walk into an Apple Store on Friday and get yourself a shiny new iPhone Duo.
Keeping up with demand
With shipping times for online preorders now slipping into 2027, it's possible there will be quite a few Apple fans interested in the iPhone Duo who are thinking about taking the walk-in retail route — but it seems stock will be very limited there too.
Before the phone was unveiled, there had been some chatter around a launch delay due to production problems, and this may be following on from that. Whatever the full story, Apple apparently can't keep up with demand for the time being.
The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable phone, and starts at $1,999 / £1,999 / AU$3,499. A quick check on the Apple site at the time of writing shows preorders scheduled to ship in January for the cheapest 256GB model in the US, UK, and Australia.

articles.title: L’IA vous fait croire à des événements qui n’ont jamais existé
articles.text:
Quelques photos retouchées par IA, un faux résumé d’une vidéo d’accident, et des centaines de volontaires ont gardé en mémoire des détails inventés de toutes pièces. Dans l’une de ces expériences, les participants ont mal répondu au test en sachant très bien que le texte sortait d’une machine.
Pattie Maes, professeure au MIT Media Lab, a montré 24 photos banales à 200 volontaires, un mariage ou une course à pied par exemple. Après une pause, une partie du groupe a revu ces images retouchées par IA, parfois animées en vidéo, avec des expressions de visage modifiées ou des personnes ajoutées dans le décor. Au test de mémoire, ces volontaires ont produit jusqu’à deux fois plus de faux souvenirs que le groupe témoin, avec davantage d’assurance dans leurs erreurs. « Je considère tout cela comme très dangereux, fondamentalement », a confié la chercheuse. Avec ces résultats, son équipe et d’autres laboratoires remettent en cause le garde-fou retenu par l’Union européenne. Dans l’AI Act, un contrôleur humain doit repérer les erreurs de la machine.
L’AI Act confie la vérification à une mémoire influençable
Mattea Sim est professeure adjointe de recherche au Massive Data Institute de l’université de Georgetown. Elle a testé ce garde-fou avec des collègues de l’université de Washington. Leurs 331 volontaires ont regardé une courte animation où une voiture rouge tourne à un carrefour, puis renverse un piéton. Un à deux jours plus tard, chacun a lu un résumé de la scène, avec le bon panneau routier ou un panneau changé par les chercheurs. Les lecteurs du résumé exact ont retrouvé le panneau de la vidéo dans 83,6 % des cas, contre 44,8 % avec la version fausse. Une partie des participants savait que le texte venait d’une IA, et leurs réponses ont été tout aussi fausses. « L’IA est un nouveau moyen de diffuser de la désinformation », prévient Mattea Sim.
Les législateurs européens ont confié à ce contrôleur humain la surveillance des systèmes d’IA à haut risque, police comprise. D’après l’article 14 du règlement, ces contrôleurs doivent pouvoir ignorer ou inverser une sortie de la machine et connaître le biais d’automatisation. En clair, un contrôleur doit savoir qu’il risque de croire une IA trop vite. Les volontaires de Georgetown le savaient, et leur souvenir de l’accident a été modifié malgré tout.
Aux États-Unis, des services de police testent des résumés d’images de caméras-piétons générés par IA, et Mattea Sim veut étudier ces rapports. En Europe, les eurodéputés et les États membres ont repoussé ces obligations au 2 décembre 2027 pour les systèmes autonomes à haut risque, dans le recrutement ou la police.
Résumés de notifications et chatbots, vos souvenirs sous influence
Si vous lisez chaque jour le résumé d’un mail ou d’une réunion préparé par un assistant IA, vous êtes à la place des volontaires de Georgetown. Au MIT Media Lab, 54 personnes chargées d’écrire des dissertations ont servi de cobayes à une autre expérience. Celles qui écrivaient avec ChatGPT ont eu nettement plus de mal à citer des passages de leur texte, quelques minutes après l’avoir rendu.
Sous le nom de la BBC, des propriétaires d’iPhone ont ainsi lu en décembre 2024 un résumé d’Apple Intelligence avec l’annonce du suicide de Luigi Mangione. L’homme, accusé du meurtre du patron d’UnitedHealthcare, était bien vivant.
Des chercheurs du MIT et de l’université de Californie à Irvine ont fait interroger des témoins d’une vidéo de crime par un chatbot et ces témoins ont produit trois fois plus de faux souvenirs que le groupe sans interrogatoire. Une autre équipe a implanté chez des volontaires le souvenir de scandales politiques inventés, avec des textes ou des deepfakes, jusqu’à réduire leur intention de vote.
Avant de retenir un chiffre ou une citation lue dans un résumé, prenez le temps d’ouvrir le texte d’origine. Apple permet aussi de désactiver ces résumés dans les réglages de notifications, application par application.
L’équipe de Pattie Maes développe en parallèle Memoro et MemPal. Avec ces deux assistants de mémoire couplés à des appareils portables, les chercheurs veulent aider des personnes âgées à retrouver une conversation oubliée ou leurs clés.

articles.title: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup After Attackers Compromise Microsoft 365 Tenants
articles.text:
ConnectWise on Saturday said it has disabled seven ConnectWise application identities as it continues its investigation into an incident in which unknown threat actors obtained unauthorized access to the application identities and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants.
The disabled identities are listed below -
- ConnectWise Cloud Backup - 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - 2399d300-6fca-4e6a-a686-399fefe75b83
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - MS Teams - 24205314-2b89-4e07-a2a4-579e898a5640
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - Exchange Online - b78f6a77-d4e5-46fb-87e5-d1648bd02519
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - MS Graph - 0de14c77-b9b0-4137-9360-34878a929827
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - Partner Center - 412dcf96-176d-4b3a-a1b0-4981ad66971e
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - SharePoint Online - b2b55f5b-7758-4719-8d8f-88ae172e6bdb
The IT management software provider said it took the action on October 17, 2026, at 07:00 UTC, adding it has also suspended Cloud Backup service by revoking certificates used for affected application connections across all users.
"Disabling the affected connections prevents new authentication through those connections; it does not reverse changes previously made inside a tenant," it said.
"The affected shared Cloud Backup credentials are no longer valid. Previously issued access tokens may remain usable until they expire or are otherwise invalidated. Any unauthorized credentials, permissions, or other access established through separate identities require additional review and remediation."
ConnectWise also noted that scheduled backups are not running, and access to affected backup archives and restoration capabilities remains unavailable. However, it emphasized that existing archives remain encrypted, isolated, and preserved, and that there is no evidence they were breached or accessed by the attackers.
Out of an abundance of caution, the company said it has temporarily taken SaaS Security and Cloud Management offline while it completes its review of the incident.
Furthermore, the company revealed that it identified the issue on October 14, 2026, through its "advanced cybersecurity monitoring and diligence," prompting it to activate internal and external incident investigation and response actions.
"Since implementing these mitigations, we have not observed successful threat activity in the environments we monitor," it said. "This finding does not establish the status of downstream customer environments, which, by design, we cannot directly observe."
At this stage, it's unclear if a product vulnerability contributed to the compromise of the application identities. The exact credential-exposure mechanism is the subject of an ongoing analysis, ConnectWise added.
The attack is particularly dangerous as it allows an attacker to abuse the application's credentials to access customers' Microsoft 365 environments without having to steal each customer's password individually. By using the stolen application credential to authenticate as that application, the attacker can request access tokens from Microsoft Entra ID based on the application's existing permissions.
Depending on the permissions assigned to the application, this could enable the attacker to potentially access other Microsoft services, including mailboxes, SharePoint documents, Teams messages, and directory information.
With ConnectWise's applications operating with extensive permissions to perform backups and management tasks, the theft of the credential allows the threat actor to authenticate as the application itself and expand their access by adding it to the Global Administrator role, adding client secrets to other trusted applications in the tenant, and creating new applications and granting them permissions.
By doing so, the client secrets offer a way to authenticate as that application and establish persistence, providing an alternative means to regain access to the compromised environment even if the original compromised credential is later revoked.
Second, Targeted Wave of Attempts Observed
"We last observed malicious sign-ins from the original address on October 15 at 08:45 UTC, with targeted, manual activity continuing until about 14:20 UTC that day," Jon Semon, Principal Security Operations Analyst at Huntress, told The Hacker News.
"ConnectWise has said access to Cloud Backup is shut off, and if so, activity through that service should have stopped. However, if the threat actor was able to add credentials to applications in Microsoft tenants, those credentials would let them keep access and act as the application."
Huntress said it has not identified new malicious activity since October 15, but there is no evidence that the stoppage was the result of public disclosure.
"We have high confidence the threat actor also targeted the ConnectWise Cloud Management apps for Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint, and we have confirmed abuse of the Teams app in one tenant," Semon said. "Those apps do not appear to have been disabled by ConnectWise, so additional activity could come from them, and we are actively investigating."
As of late Saturday, Huntress said it identified a "second, targeted wave of attempts" from the IP address "144.172.64[.]128" on October 15. These efforts, which singled out a narrow scope of 16 tenants, were unsuccessful. The tenants are in the policy, national security, trade, and critical mineral sectors.
"For the new target set, the first sweep targeted Graph tokens from the SkyKick app and occurred on October 15 between 09:25:04 and 12:35:50 UTC," Huntress said. "The second sweep hit the same tenants on the same date, between 13:54:39 and 14:20:24 UTC. This sweep appeared to be manual and targeted Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, Azure Resource Manager, Entra, and the Office 365 Management APIs."
In all, the managed security service provider has identified almost 1,000 Entra tenants with sign-in activity from the IP address associated with the unauthorized activity from the IP address in question, out of which 300 succeeded. Despite the successful sign-in, the absence of a service principal in some tenants is said to have prevented the threat actor from gaining access to those tenants.
Partners are advised to take the following actions -
- Review both their own Microsoft 365 tenant and each managed customer tenant, including environments with dormant SkyKick connections.
- Verify the status of the listed application connections and keep affected applications disabled until further notice.
- Review sign-ins across identities from October 13, 2026, through the current time, specifically for activity originating from the IP address "144.172.64[.]128."
- Preserve available sign-in and audit records before initiating containment steps.
- Review application and user authentication, application credentials and federation trusts, directory roles, owners, consent grants, and recent policy changes.
- Check for unauthorized mailbox forwarding, inbox or transport rules, and delegated mailbox access.
- Investigate any other identities changed or used during suspicious activity.
"Several Entra controls limit the damage if an application credential is stolen," Huntress said. "Application management policies can restrict or block client secrets on app registrations and cap credential lifetimes. Limiting who holds the Application Administrator and Cloud Application Administrator roles reduces who can add credentials to applications."
"Conditional Access for workload identities, which needs additional licensing, can restrict where an application is allowed to sign in from, and Microsoft Entra ID Protection can flag risky service principals. None of these replace reviewing credentials, but they make a planted secret harder to use or easier to spot."

articles.title: I tested the Lavazza Tabli, and Its eco-friendly pressed coffee tablets solve plastic pod taste and waste — even if smart home controls fall short
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Want quick and easy espresso without the waste of coffee capsules? Tired of strange-tasting coffee from plastic pods? Step this way — the Lavazza Tabli system is here to solve your problems with convenient tablets of ground, pressed coffee that are easy to use and produce delicious espresso that tastes like it could have come from fresh beans. The smartphone app is a fun touch too; just don't count on being able to start a brew through your smart speaker.
Reasons to buy
- + No coffee capsules to recycle
- + Extremely simple to use
- + Coffee tastes better than rivals like Nespresso
- + Mobile app works well, allowing customization and remote brewing
Reasons to avoid
- - Google Home connectivity didn't work during my tests
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Lavazza Tabli: 30-second review
Coffee pods are out, and tablets are in. Recently, Keurig announced that it was killing off the K-Cup in favor of compressed coffee tablets, but it wasn't the first to the punch. Italian coffee company Lavazza had debuted its own coffee tablets and brewer — the Tabli system — months before, and it's excellent.
The main appeal of Tabli's compressed coffee pucks (called tabs) is their minimal packaging — there's no metal or plastic pod that needs to be recycled after each brew or worse, end up in landfill. Using ground coffee or whole beans is a much less wasteful way to prepare an espresso, but it takes longer, and while it's a fun hobby for some of us, not everyone is interested in getting into the technicalities of brewing a balanced shot.
Each of Lavazza's tabs provides exactly the right amount of coffee for a single serving, so there's no weighing required, and no loose grounds to make a mess of your counter. The whole process is just as clean and simple as using coffee capsules, but without the empty capsules to dispose of at the end. It seems like such a simple idea that it's surprising it hasn't hit the mainstream before — and the results are very impressive.
I've become quite picky during my years reviewing coffee machines, and the Tabli system produces a better-tasting brew than any coffee capsule I've tried. Its app compatibility is a nice touch too, but the ease of use and flavor are what really count — and they're both truly impressive.
Lavazza Tabli: price and availability
- List price $129 / £199 for the machine alone
- Available as a bundle that includes a milk frother and coffee tabs
- Tabs are competitively priced and cheaper than Nespresso
The Tabli coffee machine has a list price of $129 / £199. That's between AU$190 and AU$380, though the Tabli system isn't available in Australia yet. There are also bundles available that include the Lavazza MilkEasy frother and several boxes of Tabs for much less than all the components would cost separately.
Although it's not the cheapest single-serve coffee maker around, bear in mind that unlike some of its rivals, the Tabli system won't sting you with the price of coffee in the longer term. Bosch Tassimo machines, for example, are very cheap, but the pods are some of the priciest around.
A box of 12 Tabs costs £5.89 in the UK, which is about 49p per drink. You can also pick up a multipack of eight boxes for £40, which brings the cost per drink down to 42p.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Things are slightly more expensive in the US, where you can buy a four-pack of boxes for $48, meaning each drink costs $1. That's still very reasonable, though. For comparison, Nespresso Vertuo capsules cost between $1.40 and $1.60 each.
- Value score: 4.5/5
Lavazza Tabli: specifications
| Name | Lavazza Tabli | 
| Type | Tablet coffee maker | 
| Dimensions (W x H x D) | 6.5 x 12.9 x 15.4 inches / 16.5 x 32.7 x 39cm | 
| Weight | 9.9lbs / 4.5kg | 
| Water reservoir capacity | 40.58oz / 1.2 liters | 
| Milk frother | No (but can be bought with a standalone one) | 
| Bars of pressure | 15 bar | 
| User profiles | None | 
Lavazza Tabli: design
- Sleek, modern aesthetic
- Minimalist controls
- Available in three colors
The Lavazza Tabli is a sleek-looking single-serve coffee maker that comes in three colors: graphite black (shown here), sand white, and walnut brown. The top panel has four buttons — power, single shot, double shot, and lungo — and slides back with a smooth motion to reveal the small chamber resembling the bottom of a manual espresso machine’s filter basket, where you’ll place the compressed coffee pod.
There are also warning lights that will alert you if the used tab collection bin has been removed or needs emptying, if the water tank needs filling or hasn’t been properly inserted, and if the machine needs descaling.
At the very back of the top panel, you’ll notice a flashing blue light, which indicates that the Tabli machine is ready to connect to your phone via Bluetooth. Once it’s connected, the blue light will remain steady — but more on that later.
Unlike some other Lavazza coffee machines, such as the Assoluta, the Tabli doesn’t have its own milk frothing system. However, if you’re a fan of lattes and cappuccinos, the Tabli is available bundled with a standalone frother that works extremely well. My colleague Josh Russell has just finished testing it and will be publishing his review very soon.
The Tabli has a small drip tray that’s just the right height for an espresso cup. If you want to brew into a larger cup or mug, just slide the tray out to make room. Behind the tray, you’ll find the bin into which the Tabli machine drops used coffee tabs. The tabs don’t break apart, keeping mess to a minimum, and are caught in a basket so they’re not left sitting in water.
Unlike most other coffee makers I’ve tested, the Tabli dispenses dirty water into this bin after rinsing itself rather than expelling it into the drip tray — a tidier solution that keeps the front of the machine clean.
The Tabli’s removable components aren’t dishwasher-safe, but they’re easy to hand-wash, and since this machine doesn’t have an integrated milk frother, there’s minimal maintenance necessary. Just keep the bin and drip tray clean, and follow the descaling instructions periodically.
- Design score: 5/5
Lavazza Tabli: performance
- Very simple to use
- Much better coffee than most single-serve machines
- App works well, but Google Home connectivity does not
Using the Tabli is just as simple as any ordinary capsule coffee maker: place your chosen tab in the recess under the lid, slide it closed, and pick the type of drink you want. A minute later, your drink will be ready to enjoy.
Coffee tabs are given a strength score on a scale of 1-13, and although there are currently only six types available, if the system proves successful, I'm hopeful Lavazza will increase its range.
There aren't any of the elaborate flavors you get with Nespresso or Tassimo pods; all Tabli tabs are made using nothing but compressed coffee, with no additives, and in my opinion that's no bad thing.
I've tried three Tabli varieties during testing. Qualità Rossa and Qualità Oro both produced a smooth-tasting, easy-drinking espresso, while the Espresso Ristretto was a little punchier — but not at all bitter.
None of them had the astringent taste I associate with most coffee capsules, and their taste is much more like a drink made with freshly ground coffee beans. The espresso also has a good layer of crema that beats what I've come to expect from single-serve machines.
The Lavazza Tabli has a smartphone app, which you can use to operate the machine remotely and create custom drinks. After installing the Tabli app, you’ll be prompted to create an account and then connect your coffee maker. This was quick and easy; the app will request permission to search for nearby devices, then locate the Tabli machine without the need to scan any QR codes. The first time I connected to the machine, I was prompted to grant access to my calling history and contacts, but it seems this was a temporary bug. Following an app update, I disconnected from the Tabli machine, then restarted the process, and the prompt did not appear.
The app is nicely designed, and the brewing options are presented front and center. You can choose from the machine's three brewing options or create your own, give it a name, and save it for quick access in the future. You can adjust the volume and temperature of the drink, which is particularly useful if you enjoy an Americano in the morning. Because the machine uses prepared coffee tablets rather than ground beans, if you want to change the taste any more, you’ll need to pick a different type of coffee tab,
Naturally, the app allows you to order more tabs (as well as other Lavazza products), but you have to scroll down to find the store — it’s not thrust in your face, which is refreshing.
The only issue I encountered involved the coffee maker’s smart home connectivity. The Tabli’s box advertises compatibility with Google Home and Alexa, but during my tests it sadly didn’t work. I was able to connect the Tabli machine to Google Home easily enough, but although Gemini could turn it on, it couldn’t start brewing. Nor could I use voice commands to choose different drinks, as described in the Tabli’s manual.
However, I’m not certain whether this is an issue with the Tabli or with Google Home and Gemini, which aren’t known for their flawless reliability. The Tabli app works exactly as intended, but don't count on being able to brew drinks using voice commands through a smart speaker.
- Performance score: 4.5/5
Should you buy the Lavazza Tabli?
| Lavazza Tabli score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | Not the cheapest single-serve machine, but bundles are great value and coffee tabs are very reasonably priced for better value in the long term, | 4.5/5 | 
| Design | Modern design with clean lines, which is easy to clean and maintain. Simple user interface. | 5/5 | 
| Performance | Brews delicious coffee and is very easy to use. App works well, though smart home functionality does not. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if
You hate the waste of coffee capsules
Talbi tabs are made from nothing but ground coffee, and their packaging is almost entirely cardboard, with just a thin layer of plastic over the top of the carton.
You want tasty coffee without mess
Tabli tabs are pre-measured and ground, and they don't leave residue or crumbs on your fingers. They produce a smooth, easy-drinking espresso.
Don't buy it if
You really want to experiment
Tabs are made from pre-measured and ground coffee, so you can't tinker with brew options like you can with whole beans.
You really want smart home connectivity
Google Home didn't play nicely with the Tabli during my tests, though I'm not sure whether that's an issue with Lavazza's software or Google's platform.
How I tested the Lavazza Tabli
I tested the Lavazza Tabli for three weeks, using it instead of my usual manual espresso machine. I used filtered water in its tank and used three different Tabli tab varieties. I experimented with brewing coffee remotely and creating custom drinks using the apps. I connected the coffee maker to Google Home and attempted to operate it using typed and spoken commands. I cleaned the coffee maker at the end of each day following Lavazza's instructions.
First reviewed October 2026
Cat is TechRadar's Homes Editor, covering smart home tech, kitchen appliances, vacuums, haircare and more. She's been a tech journalist for 15 years, having worked on print magazines including PC Plus and PC Format, is a Speciality Coffee Association (SCA) certified barista, and holds a professional certificate in security awareness for smart homes. Whether you want to invest in some smart lights, find your ideal hair styler, or pick the espresso machine of your dreams, she's the right person to help.

articles.title: Gratis en Steam acción y sigilo táctico: nuevo juego de PC con excelentes valoraciones
articles.text:
Intravenous 3: Borderline, un juego de acción y sigilo táctico para PC, se puede añadir gratis a la biblioteca de Steam. El título combina una perspectiva y un ritmo de combate inspirados en Hotline Miami con mecánicas asociadas a series como Metal Gear y Splinter Cell. Su llegada sin coste ofrece una opción para quienes buscan una propuesta centrada en la precisión, la infiltración y los enfrentamientos directos.
La disponibilidad resulta relevante porque el proyecto de Explosive Squat Games y HypeTrain Digital acumuló más de 360 reseñas positivas en Steam poco después de su lanzamiento, a principios de octubre.
Cuál es el nuevo juego gratuito en Steam
El protagonista de Intravenous 3: Borderline es Gideon, un hombre que trabajaba para un político corrupto. Durante ese periodo perdió todo y quedó marcado por un solo objetivo: encontrar a las personas responsables de su situación y cobrar venganza.
El juego funciona como un prólogo de Intravenous 3, una entrega más extensa que desarrolla con mayor amplitud las mecánicas de la franquicia. Sin embargo, Borderline no se limita a anticipar el contenido posterior. El título permite conocer el comienzo de la historia de Gideon y ofrece una experiencia completa e independiente.
Explosive Squat Games optó por distribuirlo como un juego gratuito para facilitar el acceso a otros títulos de la serie. Por esa razón debutó bajo el modelo free-to-play, disponible para cualquier usuario que tenga una cuenta en Steam.
La propuesta incluye dos misiones que se pueden resolver de formas distintas. El jugador puede recurrir a la acción pura, avanzar mediante el sigilo o alternar ambas opciones de acuerdo con cada situación.
Quienes prefieran los enfrentamientos directos tendrán a disposición un arsenal amplio para acabar con los enemigos. Ese camino exige precisión y rapidez, ya que cualquier error puede costar la vida del personaje. La acción remite a la intensidad de Hotline Miami, con una perspectiva que favorece decisiones rápidas durante los combates.
La alternativa táctica aprovecha influencias de Metal Gear y Splinter Cell. La oscuridad y las distracciones forman parte de las herramientas disponibles para superar los escenarios. Los entornos permiten ocultarse, distraer a los adversarios y eliminarlos poco a poco sin llamar la atención.
La duración es limitada por su condición de prólogo, pero las valoraciones de los jugadores coinciden en que se trata de una experiencia intensa y divertida para PC. El interés generado por el lanzamiento se refleja en las más de 360 opiniones positivas recibidas en la plataforma de Valve.
Cómo añadir el juego gratuito a la biblioteca de Steam
Para obtener Intravenous 3: Borderline es necesario contar con una cuenta personal en Steam. El procedimiento puede realizarse desde el programa instalado en el ordenador o desde la versión web de la tienda.
Los pasos son los siguientes:
- Iniciar sesión con la cuenta personal.
- Buscar Intravenous 3: Borderline por su nombre.
- Confirmar que el precio aparece como 0.
- Pulsar “Obtener”, “Añadir a la biblioteca” o “Jugar”.
- Comprobar que el título figure en la biblioteca digital.
En este caso, el botón “Jugar” permite incorporar el juego a la colección. Una vez añadido, el usuario puede descargarlo cuando tenga tiempo y espacio disponible en el disco duro. La recomendación es reclamar primero los títulos gratuitos y dejar la instalación para después, de modo que la capacidad del dispositivo no impida conservarlos.
Steam permite crear una biblioteca digital, recibir actualizaciones automáticas y descargar los juegos desde diferentes ordenadores asociados a la misma cuenta. La adquisición queda vinculada al perfil del usuario, por lo que el título se conserva dentro de esa biblioteca una vez añadido.
La operación representa una licencia de uso y no la compra de un producto que pueda revenderse. Los juegos no se pueden transferir a otros usuarios, y el acceso depende de las políticas y de los servidores de la plataforma.

articles.title: The Future of AI Development: Why Developers Need a Unified AI API - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence is changing how software is designed, built, and delivered. What once required specialized research teams and significant computing resources is increasingly accessible through APIs that connect applications to powerful AI models.
Developers can now integrate conversational assistants, image generation, video creation, and other intelligent capabilities into products without building every underlying system from scratch.
Yet this progress has introduced a new challenge. As the AI ecosystem expands, developers must navigate an increasingly diverse landscape of models, providers, interfaces, and technical requirements. Choosing a capable model is no longer the only consideration. Teams must also decide how to integrate it, maintain the connection, manage costs, handle failures, and adapt when a better alternative becomes available.
This is where the idea of a unified AI API becomes important. Rather than treating every model as a separate integration project, developers can adopt a more consistent approach to accessing AI capabilities. Such an approach can simplify development, support experimentation, and make applications more adaptable as the technology continues to evolve.
The Growing Complexity of AI Development
The early stages of an AI project often appear straightforward. A developer identifies a use case, finds a model that seems suitable, connects an API, and begins testing. The complexity becomes more apparent when the application grows or its requirements change.
Different AI models may expose different endpoints, accept different input formats, return different response structures, and require different authentication or configuration methods. A workflow designed around one provider may not transfer cleanly to another. Even when two models perform similar tasks, their integration requirements can vary considerably.
These differences create additional work for engineering teams. Developers may need to maintain separate client libraries, write provider-specific error handling, manage distinct credentials, and build custom logic to normalize responses. Each new integration adds another dependency that must be understood, tested, monitored, and maintained.
The challenge becomes more significant when an application uses multiple types of AI. A product might rely on a language model for planning, an image model for visual assets, and a video model for creative production. Each capability introduces its own technical considerations, making the overall architecture harder to manage.
The result is a shift in the central question facing AI developers. Instead of asking only which model offers the most useful capability, teams increasingly need to consider how their applications can access a changing collection of models without accumulating unnecessary complexity.
Why a Unified AI API Matters
A unified AI API provides a consistent access layer through which developers can work with multiple AI models. The precise implementation varies by platform, but the general objective is to reduce the amount of provider-specific work required to integrate and manage different capabilities.
This does not mean that every model becomes interchangeable. Models have different strengths, limitations, input requirements, and output characteristics. Rather, a unified interface can make the process of discovering, accessing, and integrating those capabilities more consistent.
Consider a development team building a creative application. The product may need to generate images for marketing campaigns, produce video clips for social content, and use language models to help users refine their ideas. Integrating each capability independently can lead to a fragmented architecture. A shared API layer offers a way to organize these integrations around a more coherent development experience.
For teams evaluating options, exploring platforms that bring different models into a common API environment can help clarify how this approach fits their architecture. For example, developers researching emerging generative capabilities may encounter models such as Seedance 2.5, GPT Image 2.5, and Wan 3.0 while considering how video and image generation could fit into a single application workflow.
The important consideration is not simply the number of models available. It is whether the integration approach helps developers use the right capability for a particular task while keeping the surrounding software manageable.
Model Diversity Will Shape the Next Phase of AI
AI development is unlikely to move toward a world in which one model handles every possible task equally well. Different applications demand different capabilities, and specialized models can offer distinct approaches to particular problems.
A language model may be suitable for interpreting instructions, summarizing information, or generating structured text. An image-generation model serves a different purpose, translating prompts and other supported inputs into visual content. Video-generation models introduce another set of possibilities, including workflows that involve motion, scenes, and temporal continuity. As these categories develop, developers will need to make decisions based on the actual requirements of their products. A design platform may prioritize visual consistency and control over generated assets. A marketing application may need to support both image creation and short-form video production. An educational product may combine text-based explanations with generated illustrations.
This diversity creates opportunities, but it also makes integration strategy more important. If every new model requires a separate architectural redesign, experimentation becomes expensive in engineering time and operational attention. Teams may hesitate to test potentially useful capabilities because the integration burden outweighs the immediate benefit.
A unified API can reduce that friction by separating parts of the application that define business logic from the details of individual model connections. Developers can then organize their systems around tasks and workflows rather than allowing every provider’s implementation choices to shape the entire product.
That separation becomes increasingly valuable as the market evolves and new model options emerge.
Reducing Integration Overhead Without Sacrificing Flexibility
One of the strongest arguments for a unified AI API is the opportunity to reduce repetitive engineering work. Maintaining integrations with multiple providers can involve more than writing initial request logic. Teams must also address authentication, request validation, response parsing, retries, logging, monitoring, and changes to provider-specific interfaces.
When these concerns are handled independently for every integration, they can consume time that would otherwise go toward improving the product itself.
A shared API layer can provide a more consistent foundation for these responsibilities. Developers may be able to reuse familiar request patterns, centralize parts of their error-handling logic, and apply common monitoring practices across different AI capabilities. The exact benefits depend on the platform, but the underlying objective is to make integration less fragmented.
This consistency can also help new team members become productive more quickly. Rather than learning an entirely different integration approach for each model, engineers can build on established patterns and focus on the differences that genuinely matter. The goal is to remove unnecessary complexity, not to pretend that all AI systems behave identically.
Faster Experimentation and Better Model Selection
AI development is an iterative process. The model that works well during an early prototype may not remain the best choice after user testing reveals new requirements. A product may need more consistent outputs, better handling of a particular input type, improved latency, or a different balance between quality and operating costs.
Without a flexible integration strategy, evaluating alternatives can require significant implementation work. Developers may have to modify application code, rebuild request handling, and repeat testing across several components before they can make a meaningful comparison.
A unified API can make these experiments easier to organize. When the integration layer is sufficiently consistent, teams can evaluate alternative models while keeping more of their application logic unchanged. They can compare outputs against the same test cases, investigate differences, and decide whether a change is worthwhile.
This flexibility is especially relevant to creative applications that combine several generative capabilities. A team might evaluate GPT Image 2.5 for an image-generation workflow while separately investigating Seedance 2.5 or Wan 3.0 for video-oriented use cases. The appropriate choice will depend on the capabilities each model actually supports, the application’s input requirements, and the quality of the resulting outputs.
Model selection should therefore be treated as an ongoing engineering decision rather than a one-time purchasing or implementation choice. A unified access layer can support that process, although it does not eliminate the need for careful evaluation.
Developers still need representative test data, clearly defined quality criteria, and realistic assessments of response times and operational costs. Convenience is valuable, but it should support sound technical decisions rather than replace them.
Building More Resilient AI Applications
Reliability becomes increasingly important when AI moves from an experimental feature into a core part of a production application. Users expect software to remain responsive even when an external service experiences an outage, returns an unexpected response, or reaches a usage limit.
Applications that depend heavily on a single integration may have limited options when that dependency becomes unavailable or unsuitable. A more flexible architecture can give developers additional choices, provided that alternative models can satisfy the application’s requirements.
A unified API may help teams establish consistent monitoring, error reporting, and request-management practices. Depending on the implementation, it may also simplify the process of routing suitable tasks to alternative models.
Nevertheless, switching models is not always a straightforward recovery mechanism. Different systems can produce different results, and an alternative may not support the same inputs or parameters. Applications must account for these differences through validation, testing, and clearly defined fallback behavior.
Resilience also requires attention to security. API credentials should be protected, permissions should be limited to what an application needs, and sensitive information should be handled according to appropriate data-governance policies. Centralizing access can simplify oversight, but it also makes the security practices of the shared integration layer particularly important.
A dependable AI architecture combines flexibility with deliberate controls. Developers should understand how requests are handled, what information is transmitted, how failures are reported, and what happens when a model cannot complete a task.
The Business Case for a Unified Approach
The value of a unified AI API extends beyond the engineering team. It can influence how quickly a business tests new ideas, maintains existing products, and responds to changing customer expectations.
For startups, reducing integration work may allow a small team to concentrate on the product’s defining features. For established software companies, a common access layer may help different teams follow consistent development practices. For agencies and creative studios, it can provide a more organized way to experiment with generative tools across client projects.
The financial implications require a more careful assessment. A unified API does not automatically guarantee lower costs. Actual expenses depend on the services used, the volume and complexity of requests, the models selected, and any additional infrastructure or platform charges.
Teams should evaluate the total cost of operating an AI feature rather than considering API access in isolation. Engineering maintenance, monitoring, failed requests, testing, and the work required to change providers can all affect the overall picture.
Vendor dependence is another consideration. A unified interface can reduce dependence on individual model integrations, but it may introduce dependence on the platform providing that interface. Before adopting one, developers should examine documentation quality, supported capabilities, data-handling policies, service reliability, and the practical difficulty of migrating away if requirements change.
The strongest business case emerges when the platform meaningfully simplifies the development process without introducing unacceptable trade-offs.
What Developers Should Look for in a Unified AI API
Not every unified API provides the same experience. Developers should evaluate potential solutions against the needs of their applications rather than choosing solely on the basis of a broad model catalogue.
Several considerations deserve particular attention:
- Consistent integration patterns: Determine whether common operations follow predictable conventions and whether documentation makes model-specific differences clear.
- Relevant model capabilities: Confirm that the available models support the actual tasks, inputs, and output formats required by the application.
- Transparent operational costs: Understand how usage is measured, what charges may apply, and how spending can be monitored.
- Reliability and observability: Look for useful error information, request tracking, and documentation covering service limitations and failure scenarios.
- Security and data governance: Review authentication practices, retention policies, and the handling of potentially sensitive inputs and outputs.
- Portability: Assess how much application code would need to change if the team later adopted another provider or integration method.
- Room for experimentation: Check whether developers can evaluate alternatives without rebuilding large portions of the application.
A small proof of concept is often a better starting point than an immediate commitment to a broad migration. Teams can integrate one representative workflow, test its behavior under realistic conditions, and measure the practical impact on development and maintenance.
That process helps reveal whether the abstraction genuinely saves work or merely moves complexity into another part of the system.
The Future of AI Development Is About Orchestration
As AI capabilities become more varied, successful applications will increasingly depend on how developers combine models, data, software components, and user interactions. Access to a capable model is important, but it is only one part of a complete system.
The next stage of AI development will require thoughtful orchestration: selecting appropriate models for individual tasks, coordinating their outputs, managing errors, protecting user data, and maintaining consistent application behavior. A unified AI API can provide a useful foundation for this work by reducing integration friction and making model access easier to manage.
It will not remove the need for engineering judgment. Developers must still assess quality, verify outputs, understand limitations, and design systems that behave predictably in production. Nor should a common interface obscure meaningful differences between models or lock teams into an architecture that is difficult to change.
The opportunity lies in creating software that can evolve alongside the AI ecosystem. When developers spend less time maintaining disconnected integrations, they can devote more attention to experimentation, user experience, and the problems their products are intended to solve.
In that sense, a unified AI API is not simply a convenient way to connect to multiple models. It is an architectural approach to a fast-changing field—one that prioritizes flexibility, consistency, and the ability to adapt. As new AI capabilities emerge, those qualities may prove just as important as the capabilities themselves.

articles.title: Cette peau intelligente pourrait rendre les jeux en réalité virtuelle plus immersifs
articles.text:
Pliez cette feuille de silicone conçue au MIT, et l’écran affiche presque aussitôt sa forme en 3D. Les trois chercheurs en génie mécanique qui l’ont fabriquée l’imaginent un jour cousue dans un vêtement de joueur, même si leur prototype est encore un objet de laboratoire.
Au MIT, les doctorants Qifan Yu et Nina Cao et la professeure assistante de génie mécanique Kaitlyn Becker ont glissé quatorze fibres optiques en caoutchouc dans une feuille de silicone de 16 centimètres de côté et de 5 millimètres d’épaisseur. Dans leur étude, l’écart entre la feuille réelle et sa copie numérique est inférieur à un demi-centimètre. Cousue dans un vêtement, ce type de feuille suivrait vos bras et vos jambes. Pour l'heure, au niveau de la précision, le Steam Frame de Valve, lancé en septembre, ne repère vos mouvements qu'avec ses caméras intégrées et ses deux manettes. PLeur algorithme calcule trop lentement pour un jeu vidéo et suit mal le poignet et le coude.
Du caoutchouc rugueux à la place du verre
Dans une fibre optique classique, la lumière est retenue dans un cœur en verre transparent par une gaine sombre. Plus la fibre se courbe, moins la lumière ressort à l’autre bout, et il suffit de mesurer cette perte pour estimer une courbure. Les chercheurs du MIT ont remplacé le verre par un caoutchouc souple et transparent, gainé de ce caoutchouc teint en noir, puis ils ont rendu rugueuse une seule face du cœur. Selon que la fibre plie vers cette face ou vers le côté lisse, la lumière diffuse plus ou moins, et l’équipe connaît à la fois le sens et l’ampleur de la flexion.
Les quatorze fibres sont réparties sur deux couches de sept. Chaque fibre reçoit la lumière d’une LED à une extrémité et aboutit à un capteur de lumière à l’autre. Les mesures sont ensuite collectées par une carte électronique externe, et l’algorithme de l’équipe les convertit en forme 3D.
En simulation, les chercheurs ont gagné davantage de précision en inclinant les fibres qu’en ajoutant des fibres. Ils ont aussi testé la panne de plusieurs d’entre elles. Avec trois fibres hors service sur quatorze, l’erreur simulée était inférieure à 0,3 centimètre, et elle était d’environ un centimètre, voire davantage, à partir de cinq.
Sur trois moules imprimés en 3D, l’écart entre la feuille réelle et sa reconstruction était compris entre 0,28 et 0,45 centimètre. « Les conceptions existantes, fondées sur des capteurs rigides, présentent des erreurs d’environ 1 à 2 centimètres », a précisé Qifan Yu, pour qui ce résultat est « au moins au niveau des technologies existantes ».
Un algorithme trop lent et des articulations mal suivies
Le MIT parle d’une reconstruction « presque en temps réel », mais les chercheurs obtiennent environ trois reconstructions par seconde dans MATLAB, en comptant l’ensemble de la chaîne de mesure et d’affichage. Sur le Steam Frame de Valve, lancé en septembre, l’image est rafraîchie jusqu’à 144 fois par seconde dans un mode encore expérimental. À ce rythme, la forme de la feuille ne changerait à l’écran qu’une fois toutes les 48 images environ. L’équipe envisage de remplacer le solveur généraliste du logiciel par un outil plus rapide.
Pour le MIT, la feuille est souple et extensible. D’après la description détaillée de l’étude publiée par Tom’s Hardware, la surface est entièrement souple, mais la feuille ne s’étire pas dans son ensemble. Au poignet et au coude, la peau s’étire, et l’algorithme de forme est mis en défaut par cet étirement. Les chercheurs ont donc estimé l’angle de ces articulations avec une méthode simplifiée. Un seul des auteurs a d’ailleurs réalisé toutes les démonstrations portées sur le corps.
La feuille est aussi sensible à une pression sur l’avant-bras, sans mesure calibrée de la force, et l’équipe traite cette détection à part du suivi de forme. Les fibres font aujourd’hui 1 millimètre d’épaisseur. Avec d’autres procédés de fabrication, les chercheurs pensent descendre à quelques dizaines de micromètres, soit moins qu’un cheveu, puis loger davantage de fibres dans un vêtement, par exemple pour suivre les progrès d’un patient en rééducation.
« Ces feuilles pourraient aider un kinésithérapeute à se rappeler et à comparer plus précisément le déroulement d’une évaluation aujourd’hui et celui d’il y a deux mois et des centaines de rendez-vous », a expliqué Kaitlyn Becker.

articles.title: MALFEX npm Package 'imgdecode' Hides Shellcode Loader in Windows Native Addon
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a malicious npm package that's part of a recently disclosed software supply chain attack campaign dubbed MALFEX.
The package, named "imgdecode," was uploaded to the package registry on September 30, 2026, by a user named "malfexteste8." It has been downloaded 979 times as of writing and is still available on npm as of writing. The latest version of the package is 1.0.3.
"The npm package imgdecode hides a malicious loader in a compiled Node.js addon," SafeDep said. "Its nine-line JavaScript file loads a Windows dynamic-link library (DLL). When a Node.js program calls require('imgdecode') from a Windows console, the DLL attempts to download encrypted shellcode from GitHub. It decrypts the response and injects the result into a new dllhost.exe process."
First documented by both Checkmarx and CloudSEK, MALFEX is the name assigned to a long-running campaign in which an unknown threat actor has been publishing malicious packages to npm since August 6, 2023, with an aim to compromise Windows systems. These packages were published across five npm publisher handles: malfexkkj, malfex_user, malfexteste2, malfexteste3, malfexteste4.
Of the eight identified packages, three were found to act as a loader for Overlord RAT, while three others ("cdn-img-fetch," "img-to-native," and "native-runner") worked together to download and run a Node.js stealer. A third infection pathway involved the use of a postinstall hook to execute JavaScript capable of contacting an external server and retrieving an unspecified next-stage binary.
Interestingly, the threat actor behind the campaign appears to be responding to public disclosures and npm removals by publishing replacements for "native-runner" and "img-to-native" within two days in the form of "runhelper" and "imgbundle." That same day, the first version of "imgdecode" was published. The timeline of events is as follows -
- September 26, 2026 - cdn-img-fetch, img-to-native, and native-runner 1.0.0 published
- September 28, 2026, at 4:06 p.m. UTC - npm removes native-runner and img-to-native
- September 30, 2026, at 3:29 a.m. UTC - imgbundle 1.0.0 published, replacing img-to-native
- September 30, 2026, at 3:37 a.m. UTC - runhelper 1.0.0 published, replacing native-runner
- September 30, 2026, at 4:13 p.m. UTC - runhelper unpublished
- September 30, 2026, at 10:32 p.m. UTC - imgdecode 1.0.0 published
- September 30, 2026, at 11:07 p.m. UTC - imgdecode 1.0.1 published
- October 1, 2026, at 5:48 p.m. UTC - imgdecode 1.0.2 published
- October 7, 2026, at 11:06 p.m. UTC - npm removes imgbundle
- October 8, 2026, at 1:03 p.m. UTC - npm removes cdn-img-fetch
- October 11, 2026, at 10:09 p.m. UTC - imgdecode 1.0.3 published
The Node.js stealer chain is notable for the fact that none of the packages featured an install hook. Instead, the malicious code runs when "native-runner" is loaded. The package lists "img-to-native" as its dependency, which, in turn, has "img-to-native" as a dependency.
The exact functionality of each of these packages is below -
- cdn-img-fetch downloads "banner.png" from a GitHub repository ("cavecrew/proj") and extracts an encrypted blob.
- img-to-native decrypts the blob using the key "malfexteam2027" and writes the contents to disk as a Go executable ("%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\node_runtime_helper.exe").
- native-runner executes the Go executable, which then downloads the stealer binary ("setup.exe" aka movinlike) from "104.234.65[.]75:700."
"Runhelper," advertised as a helper utility for "launching native binaries from Node.js projects," functions similarly to "native-runner" in that it's designed to run malicious code. Its primary responsibility is to locate a JPG file ("cdn-img-fetch/.runtime/rt.jpg"), extract shellcode from it, copy it into executable memory, and run it using Koffi, a Foreign Function Interface (FFI) module for Node.js.
"Six hours after runhelper was unpublished, the operator published imgdecode with a compiled DLL to run the shellcode," SafeDep said. "From version 1.0.1, the DLL also downloads and decrypts the payload. Versions 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 still call require('imgbundle') before loading the DLL. Version 1.0.3 removes that dependency and needs no other MALFEX package."
Like in the case of "runhelper," version 1.0.0 of "imgdecode" waits for "imgbundle" to write a file at the location "cdn-img-fetch/.runtime/" and, once it becomes available, reads its contents into memory, and passes them to a native Node.js addon for decoding the data.
The addon is a 64-bit Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC) DLL that first checks if it's running in a developer's terminal, and then proceeds to fetch a JPG file ("banner.jpg") from the same repository ("cavecrew/proj"), decrypt the embedded payload using the key "nif-runtime-2027," and ultimately inject the output into "dllhost.exe."
"After decryption, the DLL checks the first bytes of the plaintext," SafeDep explained. "If they match a JPEG or PNG signature, the DLL stops. Inference: the operator could turn the loader off by serving encrypted content that decrypts to an image. Serving an ordinary image would instead generally cause decryption to fail before this check."
Although the GitHub account "cavecrew" is no longer accessible, an Internet Archive screenshot of the image file dated October 6, 2026, shows that it contains the same Go-based downloader used for retrieving the Node.js stealer and remote access tool ("movinlike") from "104.234.65[.]75:700."
The Node.js application includes a .env file containing a command-and-control (C2) address ("104.234.65[.]75:7007") and a MALFEX license key, indicating the use of a malware builder or licensing system to craft such payloads.
The malware runs anti-analysis checks that audit for the presence of virtual machines, sandboxes, and analysis tools like Process Monitor and Wireshark, before harvesting files matching seed phrases and specific extensions (.kdbx, .pem, .ppk, and .env), as well as data from Chromium-based web browsers, Discord, Telegram, cryptocurrency wallets, and gaming apps (Steam, Epic Games, Riot, Battle.net, Minecraft, and Ubisoft).
It can also establish a WebSocket connection to the C2 server, allowing it to accept commands for shell execution, file transfer, process control, clipboard access, screenshots, and mouse and keyboard input. For persistence, it adds a Registry Run key and creates a scheduled task named "MicrosoftEdgeUpdateService."
Developers who have installed any of the aforementioned packages should treat their Windows systems as potentially compromised, isolate them, check for persistence entries, rotate credentials, and transfer funds to new wallets if seed phrases were stored in them.

articles.title: Por qué no se debe limpiar la pantalla del celular con ropa o papel de cocina y cuál es la mejor opción
articles.text:
La pantalla del celular es una de las superficies que más tocamos a diario, y con ella llegan huellas, polvo y grasa que muchos intentan eliminar con lo primero que tienen a mano: una camiseta o un trozo de papel de cocina.
Esa costumbre, sin embargo, puede terminar dañando el dispositivo de forma permanente. Los materiales cotidianos no están diseñados para superficies delicadas y, con el tiempo, desgastan la capa protectora del cristal.
Por qué la ropa y el papel de cocina dañan la pantalla
Sobre el panel de los teléfonos existe un recubrimiento oleofóbico que repele la grasa y evita que las huellas se adhieran con facilidad. Apple señala que los productos y materiales abrasivos pueden reducir las propiedades de este recubrimiento y dañar el dispositivo.
Una camiseta parece inofensiva, pero el tejido suele acumular polvo y partículas de suciedad entre la tela y la pantalla. Al frotar, esas partículas generan fricción y pueden provocar microrayones tanto en el panel como en la cobertura de los objetivos de las cámaras.
El papel de cocina presenta un problema similar. Aunque a simple vista resulte suave, su superficie tiene una dureza mayor a la que parece, lo que lo vuelve perjudicial para el cristal. Lo mismo ocurre con el papel higiénico y con cualquier tejido cuya composición y nivel de abrasión se desconozcan.
¿Por qué no conviene limpiar la pantalla del celular con ropa o papel de cocina? Porque ambos materiales no están diseñados para superficies delicadas: arrastran partículas de polvo que generan fricción, desgastan el recubrimiento oleofóbico que repele la grasa y pueden provocar microrayones permanentes en el cristal, incluso en modelos protegidos con vidrios resistentes.
El desgaste del recubrimiento no afecta el funcionamiento del teléfono, pero sí su capacidad para repeler la grasa. Con el tiempo, la pantalla retiene más huellas y se ensucia con mayor facilidad, lo que lleva a una limpieza más frecuente y, en consecuencia, a un deterioro mayor.
Otros materiales y productos que también se deben evitar
Más allá de la ropa y el papel, existen prácticas igual de riesgosas. Expertos consultados por Xataka recomiendan no utilizar objetos punzantes ni metálicos para retirar suciedad endurecida, como restos de alimentos pegados al cristal, porque pueden afectar la pantalla o dañar componentes internos del equipo. En esos casos, lo adecuado es humedecer la zona con agua para ablandar la mugre antes de limpiarla.
Tampoco se recomienda el uso de líquidos abrasivos como limpiacristales, abrillantadores de muebles, acetona o disolventes, ya que contienen sustancias que deterioran las capas protectoras del dispositivo. El alcohol que se vende comúnmente en farmacias también debe evitarse, por ser demasiado concentrado o contener aditivos no aptos para pantallas.
Los paños ásperos o que sueltan pelusa completan la lista de elementos a descartar, porque dejan residuos y pueden generar marcas adicionales. Cabe recordar que las pantallas modernas suelen contar con protecciones como el Gorilla Glass, pensadas para resistir caídas y rayones, pero que no son inmunes al desgaste, algo que el youtuber JerryRigEverything demostró en reiteradas pruebas de resistencia.
Cómo limpiar la pantalla del celular de forma segura
El primer paso consiste en bloquear o apagar el dispositivo, lo que permite identificar mejor la suciedad acumulada sobre el cristal.
Después debe emplearse un paño de microfibra limpio, similar al que se usa para gafas o cámaras fotográficas, con movimientos suaves y sin aplicar presión excesiva. Este paño se ensucia con el uso, por lo que conviene lavarlo o reemplazarlo cada cierto tiempo.
En casos de mayor suciedad, se puede recurrir a alcohol isopropílico de al menos 90%, aplicado directamente sobre el paño y nunca sobre la pantalla. Este producto es recomendable porque se evapora con rapidez y no deja residuos sobre la superficie.
Tras eliminar las manchas, conviene pasar un paño seco para retirar cualquier resto de humedad y dejar el cristal completamente seco. Estos mismos elementos, microfibra y alcohol isopropílico, también sirven para limpiar computadoras, tablets y teclados sin comprometer sus superficies.

articles.title: Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers are sounding the alarm related to an active campaign in which unknown threat actors are abusing a compromised Microsoft 365 (M365) credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) to gain unauthorized access to customers' M365 environments.
ConnectWise Cloud Backup is a cloud-based backup and recovery service built for managed service providers (MSPs) to secure their clients' Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace data. To accomplish its tasks, the application is granted broad access to mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and directory data in every tenant on which it's installed.
Huntress said it has observed confirmed unauthorized sign-ins within 173 partner/customer tenants using the compromised vendor credential. The incident impacts every organization that has the app installed, and the credential works against every tenant the app is consented in.
"The app's credential is in hostile hands," security researcher Jonathan Semon said. "It was used to obtain Microsoft Graph tokens in customer tenants from 144.172.64[.]128 on October 15, between 06:13 and 08:34 UTC. The actor moved through tenants in sorted GUID order, a few seconds apart, which points to a script working from a target list."
In the observed attackers, the adversary has been observed authenticating to the app using their own tooling, in a manner analogous to the backup service, and obtains tokens with the app's existing permissions. Given that the app has extensive permissions to access customer data, an attacker in possession of the tokens can read mailboxes, files, and directory data the backup service can.
Huntress said the same IP address engaged in password spraying against four law firm tenants on October 13 and 14, 2026, although it said it detected no successful user sign-ins in its telemetry.
In at least one partner tenant, the cybersecurity company said it found a separate ConnectWise app assigning itself Global Administrator privileges and adding credentials to other trusted applications within this environment, thereby opening a pathway to other privileged apps within customer environments. This effectively extends the risk beyond the vendor account.
"The ConnectWise Cloud Management app for Microsoft Teams (application ID 24205314-2b89-4e07-a2a4-579e898a5640) added itself to the Global Administrator role, then ran a Python script (User-Agent Python-urllib/3.12) that modified two other applications in the tenant: an MSP management application, and Huntress's own application (Huntress Security Platform), adding new client secrets to both," Semon explained.
"The two applications that received new secrets are trusted, privileged tools. Adding a credential to an MSP management application can extend access beyond the one tenant, because those applications are often consented into the MSP's customers' tenants. A credential on a security tool's application gives the holder whatever that tool is permitted to do."
Todyl, in a similar analysis, said it detected an unauthorized party authenticating to Microsoft Graph as the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application.
"The access inherited the app's existing consent, which permits read/write access to mail and attachments (full mailbox access through Exchange Web Services), OneDrive and SharePoint files, and Teams chats, including the ability to restore data," Nicholas Koken, Todyl's head of Detection Engineering, said.
"Revoking user sessions does not end this access. Disabling the app in a tenant stops new tokens from being issued there, though tokens already issued stay valid for up to 90 minutes. Any tenant where the app is still enabled stays exposed until ConnectWise rotates the credential."
In response to the incident, ConnectWise has taken the step of closing Cloud Backup application access until further notice. The company said it has found no evidence that Cloud Backup partner backup data has been compromised. It has also shared the following steps to look for indicators of compromise -
- In the Microsoft Entra Admin Center, navigate to Monitoring → Sign-in logs, select the Service principal sign-ins tab, and filter by Application ID 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae.
- The default User sign-ins tab will not display the required information.
- In the IP address column, review authentication activity originating from IP addresses outside expected Microsoft/Azure ranges. The application's normal egress has been identified as Azure private IPv6.
- Suspicious IP address: 144.172.64[.]128
"The backup service needs broad access to do its job, and an attacker using its credentials will inherit that level of access for every tenant where the app is installed," Huntress explained.
"Depending on the permissions in the tenant, that can include mailboxes, OneDrive and SharePoint files, Teams data, and directory information, much of it belonging to your clients. Some of that access, such as directory reads through Microsoft Graph, leaves no audit trail, which is why we suggest acting now instead of waiting for proof of access. The full potential impact depends on the permissions in play in each tenant."
Users are recommended to disable the application until ConnectWise confirms all credentials have been reset, enable Microsoft Graph activity logs, audit for any new credentials added since October 13, 2026, and check Entra audit logs for ConnectWise or SkyKick applications adding themselves to a directory role.
The development comes as Google's Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group, along with ManageEngine Threat Analysis Lab, detailed an "ephemeral supply chain tampering" of the update infrastructure belonging to AOMEI Backupper, a data backup, disk cloning, and disaster recovery software, to bypass traditional security defenses and deliver malware such as CROSSROAD and SHINYROAD.
"The threat actor conducted repeated, short-burst configuration tampering against AOMEI origin servers," Google said. "Each tampering window remained active for only five to ten minutes before reverting to authentic versions. During the brief tampering windows, the threat actor modified the update settings file on the update server to redirect the software to download a malicious ZIP package from attacker-controlled servers instead of legitimate updates."
The ZIP archive contains CROSSROAD, an initial downloader responsible for environment validation and staging follow-on payloads. It's also designed to establish scheduled task-based persistence to deploy SHINYROAD, a modular backdoor framework for covert command-and-control, via DLL sideloading.
The software supply chain compromise campaign, which occurred between April and July 2026, has been attributed to a previously undocumented threat cluster codenamed UNC7017. The activity marks the first time that such a compromise has played out in brief intervals instead of maintaining a persistent, static modification on the servers.
The campaign is assessed to have impacted organizations spanning a wide range of sectors, including IT services, telecommunications, higher education, and related entities in Australia, Brazil, India, Pakistan, Portugal, Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, Türkiye, and the U.S.
An Active Supply Chain Attack
In a post on X, Microsoft said it's tracking an "active supply chain attack in which a threat actor compromised the trusted OAuth App of the backup application ConnectWise Cloud Backup (AppId: 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae), formerly SkyKick Backup, to obtain access tokens across customer tenants."
The tech giant said the threat actor likely abused permissions previously granted by customers to the application, including highly privileged permissions like Directory.ReadWrite.All.
"On October 15, 2026, we observed broad successful service principal authentication originating from the IP address 144.172.64[.]128," it added. "Follow-on activity included Microsoft Graph API reconnaissance and attempts to add additional credentials on the related service principal in target tenants to maintain direct access as a backdoor."
Microsoft is recommending that security teams review service principal sign-ins from unrecognized IP addresses, app credential changes, and OAuth grant activity associated with the aforementioned OAuth AppId.
ConnectWise, in a separate advisory, confirmed it has identified unauthorized access to application identities within the ConnectWise Cloud Backup environment. It has shut off Cloud Backup application access while its "investigation and remediation efforts remain ongoing."
Listed below are the application IDs the threat actor has abused as part of the activity -
- ConnectWise Cloud Backup - 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - 2399d300-6fca-4e6a-a686-399fefe75b83
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - MS Teams - 24205314-2b89-4e07-a2a4-579e898a5640
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - Exchange Online - b78f6a77-d4e5-46fb-87e5-d1648bd02519
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - MS Graph - 0de14c77-b9b0-4137-9360-34878a929827
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - Partner Center - 412dcf96-176d-4b3a-a1b0-4981ad66971e
- ConnectWise Cloud Management - SharePoint Online - b2b55f5b-7758-4719-8d8f-88ae172e6bdb
"When it comes to early exploitation and post-exploitation behaviors, we've observed what might be an affinity towards alphabetical targeting (our most interesting victims start with 'A')," Huntress said. "Although all tenants should be scrutinized, this pattern is worth sharing for prioritization."
