articles.title: ixigo Q2 profit at Rs 63 Cr on robust show in hotel booking biz
articles.text:
ixigo Q2 profit at Rs 63 Cr on robust show in hotel booking biz
This was aided by the partial sale of stake in Freshbus and strong growth in the hotel bookings segment.
ixigo (Le Travenues Technology Limited) has reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 63.42 crore for the September quarter, aided by the partial sale of stake in Freshbus, an intercity electric bus operator and smart mobility startup, and strong growth in the hotel bookings segment.
The travel and ticket booking platform had posted a net loss of Rs 3.46 crore in the corresponding July-September period of the last financial year, as per a regulatory filing.
Hotels emerged as ixigo's fastest-growing business line by gross transaction value (GTV), reaching Rs 111.34 crore, up 159 per cent YoY, ixigo stated. This is the first time ixigo has reported hotels as a separate line of business.
During the second quarter of 2026-27, ixigo's revenue from operations increased to Rs 320.96 crore from Rs 284.23 crore a year ago. Total expenses were higher at Rs 309.51 crore as against Rs 291.89 crore.
"In Q2 FY27, we delivered resilient growth with quarterly gross transaction value (GTV) of Rs 5,304 crore, up 22 per cent YoY, and revenue from operations of Rs 321 crore, up 13 per cent YoY. Our PAT (profit after tax) was an all-time high aided by our partial sale of stake in Freshbus," ixigo Group CEO Aloke Bajpai, Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar, and Group CFO Saurabh Devendra Singh said in a joint statement.
"We continue to invest in Hotels and AI as key drivers of our long-term growth," they further stated.

articles.title: Why BioWare's Neverwinter Nights still has thousands of active players
articles.text:
Neverwinter Nights was made by the studio that produced seminal RPGs Baldur’s Gate, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age. It sold well and was critically acclaimed at launch. Yet, somehow, it has not been canonized in most gamers’ minds over the decades the same way the games that came before and after it were.
Nonetheless, more than two decades later, it still has a tight-knit and surprisingly active community that none of those other games can rival. I think that’s partly because it was a completely different beast.
BioWare is known for making multi-character, story-driven role-playing games that focused primarily on single-player story campaigns, though some supported co-op play in those campaigns. With Neverwinter Nights, BioWare instead made a game that was as focused on a modding toolset for content creation as it was on giving players a pre-packaged story, and that emphasized multiplayer at least as much as solo play.
Today you would expect this to be a calculated attempt to bring more long-term, always-on, multiplayer-as-a-service to an RPG franchise that has mostly appealed to solo players. You might imagine it would be about selling cosmetics, a subscription, or a battle pass, or maybe you would think it was about nabbing appealing engagement numbers.
But it’s clear from playing it today that Neverwinter Nights wasn’t primarily made for those reasons. Instead, it came from a passion for tabletop role-playing and a desire to get closer to that in video game form than ever before.
Yes, the BioWare team noted in some interviews that they saw this as a trial run for exploring the idea of making a massively multiplayer game (MMO)—something that, in the year 2000, was seen by many as the hot new business opportunity in gaming, and which was in many ways the precursor to the games-as-a-service we see today. They then indicated they realized that an MMO was harder to make than they had assumed and abandoned that ambition well before Neverwinter Nights shipped.
Neverwinter Nights is not exactly an MMO. Instead, it’s designed for small communities of people to inhabit and create with, and it features a powerful toolset for virtual dungeon masters to use to subject regular players to challenges in an improvisational way on a live server.
“We always envisioned it as a table with four legs—the single player, the multiplayer, the DMing tools and the toolset (the module making tools),” BioWare’s Ray Muzyka told IGN around the time the game was released. “They all appeal to different groups, and we’ve tried to make them all equivalently high quality.”
Over the past month, I’ve been replaying Neverwinter Nights‘ main story campaign, The Wailing Death, as a solo player, for the first time in 20 years. The nostalgia has been strong in this replay, but I have also found that BioWare didn’t quite nail “equivalently high quality” for all the pillars. Still, it doesn’t matter, because as we’ll see when we check in with the game’s community, the campaign is not the point.
“The single player experience has to be as good as anything we’ve ever done in [Baldur’s Gate], [Baldur’s Gate 2], or Throne of Bhaal and hopefully better,” Muzyka told IGN. “Our goal here at BioWare is that each game we do has to be better than the previous one.”
If single-player is one of the legs, it might be fair to call Neverwinter Nights‘ table a little wobbly. It still stands, but you know how irritating it can be.
For example, Neverwinter Nights leaves behind Baldur’s Gate or Icewind Dale‘s party-based systems, and instead has the player controlling just one character directly. It makes sense for a multiplayer game, but doesn’t work as well for a single-player experience in this case—at least with the Dungeons & Dragons rules of the time.
I chose to play a monk, a martial arts specialist, simply because I’ve always been drawn to that particular fantasy identity, and because I’d never played one in a D&D game. I regretted that decision after a while.
For many of the character levels covered in The Wailing Death, the monk basically just picks between two fighting modes: one that misses more but attacks more frequently, and one that’s just normal. That, along with some intense restrictions on which weapons or armor can be used while keeping all their benefits, and a couple of knockdown and stun attacks that often don’t work, make up the whole kit for many hours of playtime, particularly in the first act. (It does get better later on, though.)
The original campaign is fun and nostalgic, but it’s arguably not BioWare’s best.
The original campaign is fun and nostalgic, but it’s arguably not BioWare’s best.
Credit:
GOG
A kit like this makes sense in a pen-and-paper RPG with a live dungeon master (DM), because the player and DM can work together to invent creative expressions of their abilities, and it works in a party in a video game because it’s just one of multiple complementary characters with a wide range of skills and spells.
But for a game that is about 80 percent battling enemies without controlling any other characters, it gets monotonous quickly. There aren’t as many meaningful character builds, gearing, or tactical choices as you’re used to in some other RPGs until quite a ways into the campaign. Often, you just run in and watch the dice roll until either you die or the enemy dies, while sometimes drinking potions.
This problem is less severe with some other classes, but the tension is usually there to some degree.
Whereas Baldur’s Gate 2, for example, had a partial authored background for your character that then played into the narrative, Neverwinter Nights leaves you as an Elder Scrolls-like blank slate. I normally love that! It’s good for role-playing with friends, because you can make up your own character completely. But it means the story can’t be character-driven, and the gameplay doesn’t provide enough flexibility or freedom in return.
Still, I enjoyed my experience with the campaign when I replayed it recently, even if it couldn’t match Baldur’s Gate 2, Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, or other BioWare classics for me personally. While the story wasn’t anything special by BioWare’s standards, there was something genuinely cozy to me about the genericness of the narrative. It took me back to an earlier time in CRPGs, before things got quite so precious. “This is just like D&D!” was still enough to sell it on its own. Maybe it’s just nostalgia, though.
Since most people played the game solo, and it was a relatively small portion of the player base that dove deep into the construction kit or DM tools, I think this is the main reason Neverwinter Nights has not achieved the same pantheon status as other BioWare titles that came before and after it.
But for those lucky few who were invested in those other table legs, it actually was quite special—and amazingly, it remains so today.
The persistent worlds of Neverwinter Nights
“The main thing I would shout from the rooftops if I could, is that firing up Neverwinter Nights and launching its original campaign… does not do justice to what Neverwinter Nights has become since,” a longtime player named Daniel Morris told me. He goes by Irongron in the community, and he runs Arelith, which is both one of the OG persistent multiplayer servers and one of the most popular servers today. Morris is also working on a visual overhaul of the original campaign; he hopes to release it next year.
Arelith hit its peak player count “a little less than two years ago,” as Morris tells it—not way back when the game was new. “Our community is the heart of Arelith, it’s not just our audience, but where we find our DMs and developers,” he said.
Arelith is a fountain of creativity; for example, this is original artwork commissioned for the game’s loading screens from artist Matheus Graef.
Arelith is a fountain of creativity; for example, this is original artwork commissioned for the game’s loading screens from artist Matheus Graef.
Credit:
Matheus Graef
I spent many evenings in my younger days playing multi-user dungeons (MUDs), the text-based online role-playing games that preceded MMOs like EverQuest or World of Warcraft. While there were big MUDs, many were small communities of just one or two dozen people, and often, those same people were the ones actually making the game’s content. For example, I was a room builder for one MUD; I wrote the descriptions for places in the MUD’s world and decided which monsters, NPCs, or items inhabited those places.
Neverwinter Nights‘ multiplayer platform and community—both as it was back in the 2000s and as it is today—reminds me of those MUD days. There’s an ownership of that shared world that is entirely lost in the MMO days, perhaps more akin to a modern, small Minecraft server than an MMO with thousands of users.
That seems to be part of the appeal for a player I spoke with who goes by the name NelaK in the community, and who has, among other things, taken over maintenance and moderation of the Neverwinter Vault, the community’s de facto hub for two decades. The website hosts news, patches, assets, mods, a forum, a wiki, and an associated Discord server.
“It’s not an MMO, and that’s a good thing in my opinion. The communities are smaller, which means your roleplay and your actions matter and can affect the world,” said NelaK. “The world itself can be tailored around what the players want. That’s a unique thing that you can’t get from an MMO or from smaller-scale multiplayer games. It sits in a sweet spot where you can have enough players that it feels like a proper community and a world you can engage with while you can still matter.”
Baldur’s Gate and Icewind Dale did have multiplayer, where each player could control one or more characters directly. As noted, Neverwinter Nights limits each player to one character, but it adds a new role: a dungeon master, who can spawn enemies, occupy and act as NPCs, and more, to aid in group storytelling, similar to a pen-and-paper game.
“While Arelith is essentially a mini MMO, many of the other servers pride themselves in running highly curated, beautifully crafted campaign worlds much closer to tabletop role-playing game emulator that Neverwinter Nights was first intended as,” Morris told me. He called Neverwinter Nights “a direct translation of the tabletop role-playing game experience into the digital sphere.”
It’s as much a construction kit as it is a game
The game’s modding kit and easy-to-use scripting tools let players build scenarios relatively quickly. It essentially let players build a little RPG world, run it, and inhabit it. It was a bustling scene back then, and there’s still a community doing this today. The combination of the relative simplicity of the graphics and the elegance of the tools make this toolset an unusually excellent balance between flexible, powerful, and easy to learn.
“The tile-based areas are basic and limiting in some respects, but they do mean that building areas is quick and easy,” explained NelaK. “It’s much more approachable than a lot of other platforms.”
For NelaK and some other members of the game’s community today, the game’s tools aren’t just the remaining appeal—they’re the main appeal.
“I’ve been playing Neverwinter Nights since launch day. I remember one of my friends dragging me along to the store because they really wanted the game and I went just to keep them company,” he remembered. “I ended up buying it, and I’ve been hooked ever since, but to this day, I’ve still never played through the original campaigns… and yet I’ve played Neverwinter Nights or spent time building or working on something Neverwinter Nights-related most days since.”
I toyed around with the tools quite a bit back in the day. I remember re-creating a big chunk of the world of my favorite MMO at the time, Meridian 59, with the intent to make a story-driven, single-player campaign for that game; Meridian 59 had very little narrative as it was.
I also remember that Neverwinter Nights was for many years a common way for would-be narrative designers to make a portfolio piece for applying for jobs within the games industry. When I was in college, a close friend of mine (Brian “Psychochild” Green, who at the time co-ran Meridian 59, and sadly has since passed) offered to show my Neverwinter Nights modules to some friends of his at BioWare if I wanted to interview for a job there to write for their next game, which, based on timing, probably would have been Mass Effect. I declined in order to focus on other priorities I had at the time, for better or worse.
Similarly, many (though certainly not all) people in the community have professional backgrounds closely related to, or at least adjacent to, game development.
“Neverwinter Nights provides a unique intersection of where I can apply my technical and professional skills along with my interest in video games and do it for something that doesn’t feel like work,” said NelaK. Morris specifically noted that several members of the Arileth team work or have worked in the games industry or software development.
This is the game’s legacy, not the story campaigns that shipped with the game. And that explains the game’s relative obscurity today: that’s a more niche appeal than a really good, story-driven, single-player RPG. But for the people who are into it, there’s nothing else that quite compares.
Returning to Neverwinter Nights today
I don’t imagine most people still regularly see references to Neverwinter Nights, but I sometimes do. For the past couple of years, I’ve enjoyed the dark fantasy trend on TikTok. These are short, vertical videos set to a particular kind of 1980s fantasy-type medieval synth music, depicting imagery from what feels like a long-lost, strangely nostalgic subgenre of fantasy media that is more implied in our memories’ liminal space between real fantasy movies and books of the ’80s and early ’90s than it is something that actually specifically existed.
It turns out Neverwinter Nights‘ assets fit that milieu quite well, so I sometimes saw videos of people creating online Neverwinter Nights servers meant to capture that vibe. It’s niche as hell, but it’s there. The TikTok videos from one of the game’s servers were actually how I got inspired to try the game again.
“Over the last year there’s been a bit of a resurgence, with new servers going live, and others going viral,” Morris told me. Some player-run servers “have had hundreds of thousands interacting with their TikTok videos.”
He added that his own community’s Discord server has 5,000 members, and that’s just one part of the game’s wider audience.
If you want to get back into the game or try it for the first time, you can buy the Enhanced Edition on GOG and other storefronts; a front-page poll on the Neverwinter Vault indicates that about 65 percent of the community primarily uses that version, as compared to previous releases or the sequel, Neverwinter Nights 2.
If you want to try the single-player, the Enhanced Edition comes with a plethora of officially sanctioned campaigns of varying quality—not just The Wailing Death.
But let’s say you, like some members of the game’s current community, are more interested in multiplayer than single-player. A good place to start is the Neverwinter Vault. Additionally, Enhanced Edition developer Beamdog hosts a list of active community servers you can join.
As I write this, a few hundred people are playing across a couple dozen servers, which is impressive. I love to see old games like this keep the community going. It’s especially important for Neverwinter Nights, because more than any other BioWare game or even most other RPGs in general, this game is its community.

articles.title: NixOS statt Microsoft: Wie die Niederlande ihre digitale Souveränität erzwingen
articles.text:
NixOS statt Microsoft: Wie die Niederlande ihre Behörden-IT unabhängig von den USA machen
Die Niederlande entwickeln einen eigenen Behördendesktop auf Basis freier Software. Das Projekt trägt den Namen DAWO, kurz für „Digitaal Autonome Werkomgeving Overheid“ – also „digital autonome Arbeitsumgebung der Regierung“. Als Betriebssystem hat sich der Staat für die Linux-Distribution NixOS entschieden. Acht Kommunen in dem Land testen das System bereits in der Praxis, organisiert über den Gemeindeverband VNG. DAWO ist dabei kein fertiges Produkt, sondern eher eine Art Bauplan: Er beschreibt eine komplette Arbeitsumgebung aus austauschbaren Bausteinen für Betriebssystem, Cloudinfrastruktur, Kommunikation, KI und gemeinsames Arbeiten an Dokumenten, wobei es stets um Souveränität geht.
Drei staatliche IT-Dienstleister entwickeln
Im Juli 2026 beauftragte die zuständige „interdepartementale Kommission für den Geschäftsbetrieb des Staatsdienstes“ (ICBR) drei staatliche IT-Dienstleister mit der Umsetzung: SSC-ICT, DICTU und DUO-ICT. Die übergeordnete Blaupause für das Projekt kommt aus dem Ministerium für Inneres. Beim Betriebssystem für die Arbeitsplatzrechner probierte das Projekt zunächst openSUSE und Fedora aus, entschied sich dann aber für NixOS.
Ein zentraler Baustein dabei ist „MijnBureau“, eine von den Behörden selbst betriebene Suite für den Arbeitsplatz. Sie kombiniert Nextcloud für Dateien, Collabora für Office-Aufgaben, Element für die Kommunikation und OpenProject für das Projektmanagement. Hier läuft das Vorhaben auch schon europäisch: Das Team hinter MijnBureau arbeitet mit dem französischen Projekt La Suite zusammen und orientiert sich an openDesk, dem entsprechenden Vorhaben in Deutschland.
US-Sanktionen als Beschleuniger
Den Anstoß für DAWO gab laut dem niederländischen Tech-Portal Tweakers unter anderem die Erfahrung mit US-Sanktionen gegen den Internationalen Strafgerichtshof (ICC) in Den Haag. Microsoft kappte damals das E-Mail-Konto des damaligen Chefanklägers Karim Khan auf Druck der US-Regierung.
Der Fall zeigte, dass der Zugang zu wichtigen digitalen Werkzeugen von politischen Entscheidungen anderer Länder abhängen kann. Dieses Risiko will die niederländische Regierung offenbar nicht länger eingehen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 30.09.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
Oh, jetzt plötzlich wird nachgedacht? Emailadressen die von Internetprovidern zur Verfügung gestellt sind werden gerne an den Bezug von Diensten dieses Providers gekoppelt.Kündigt man dem Provider ist – manchmal ohne Vorwarnung- die Adresse weg !Natürlich erfolgt keine Verständigung des Providers ! Dann kannst Du nicht mal ummelden, da die alte Adresse als Verifikation nicht mehr zur Verfügung steht. Auch die am Server gebliebenen Mails sind dann weg. Hat bislang aber noch keinen gestört !

articles.title: Apple bannit de l'App Store les fonctions cachées et les applis de nudification par IA
articles.text:
Apple a modifié son règlement d’examen des applications pour s’attaquer aux outils d’IA capables de déshabiller une personne réelle sur une photo. Les éditeurs qui présentent une appli anodine à ses équipes avant d’activer une fonction cachée risquent désormais le retrait de l’App Store et la résiliation de leur compte développeur.
Au tournant de l’année, des milliers d’internautes ont demandé à l’assistant Grok d’Elon Musk de dénuder des femmes et des mineures sur X. Apple n’a rien dit en public, mais a menacé xAI de retirer Grok de l’App Store en janvier, avant de valider une version corrigée de l’appli. La firme de Cupertino vient de réécrire ses règles. Les images intimes non consenties, y compris celles générées par IA, sont citées noir sur blanc à l’article 1.2, et un nouvel article 2.5.19 bannit toute fonction cachée. Apple durcit le texte, mais les éditeurs d’applis de « nudification » ont surtout profité des failles de son examen et de la vitrine de l’App Store.
Apple interdit les applis à double fond
« N’incluez aucune fonctionnalité cachée, dormante ou non documentée dans votre application », exige désormais Apple dans son règlement. Les développeurs qui tentent de masquer ces fonctions dans le code de leur appli, par obfuscation ou par une autre méthode, risquent le retrait de l’App Store et la résiliation de leur compte. Avec l’obfuscation, un éditeur rend son code illisible et cache son véritable fonctionnement aux équipes d’examen. L’article 2.3.1 interdisait en réalité les fonctions cachées, mais Apple a voulu une règle plus explicite et nomme la « nudification » dans sa note aux développeurs.
L’éditeur soumet à l’examen une appli inoffensive et ne révèle sa fonction de « nudification » qu’après validation. Apple appelle cette tactique « bait-and-switch ». Ses équipes ont trouvé l’an dernier des fonctions cachées dans 22 000 soumissions, et Apple a retiré près de 59 000 applis validées en tant que jeux ou utilitaires, puis transformées en outils d’escroquerie après leur approbation.
Les éditeurs peuvent aussi jouer sur la localisation de leurs utilisateurs. 9to5Mac a ainsi découvert en juillet sur l’App Store brésilien des dizaines de plateformes de paris déguisées en jeux et en utilitaires, dont beaucoup étaient accessibles aux enfants. Hors du Brésil, ces applis fonctionnaient normalement, et la plateforme de paris n’apparaissait qu’aux internautes connectés depuis une adresse IP brésilienne.
Apple a également réécrit la section 5 de son règlement. Les applis qui facilitent la traite d’êtres humains ou l’exploitation d’enfants, interdites de longue date sur l’App Store, seront aussi bloquées sur les canaux de distribution alternatifs, ouverts en Europe par le DMA.
- Interface fluide et intuitive
- Sécurité des apps vérifiée
- Intégration avec iCloud
Apple laisse de côté son moteur de recherche
À l’article 1.2, Apple demande aux éditeurs d’applis de création ou de partage de contenus d’empêcher la publication d’images intimes non consenties et de les retirer sans attendre de signalement. Ceux qui n’installent pas de garde-fous suffisants, ou ne corrigent pas une infraction après notification, risquent d’enfreindre le code de conduite des développeurs et de voir leur appli retirée.
Le Tech Transparency Project est une ONG américaine spécialisée dans les enquêtes sur les géants de la tech. Elle a trouvé en janvier 47 applis de « nudification » sur l’App Store et 55 sur Google Play, avec plus de 700 millions de téléchargements et 117 millions de dollars de revenus au total. Apple et Google prélèvent une commission sur ces revenus, et Apple a retiré 28 de ces applis après la publication. « Grok n’est vraiment que la partie émergée de l’iceberg », avait alors prévenu Katie Paul, directrice de l’ONG, dans un entretien à la presse britannique.
Trois mois plus tard, l’ONG a montré qu’Apple orientait directement les internautes vers ces applis, avec ses suggestions de recherche et ses publicités. Quand l’ONG tapait « AI NS », Apple lui suggérait la recherche « image to video ai nsfw », et plusieurs applis de « nudification » apparaissaient dans les dix premiers résultats. Apple a retiré 15 applis signalées. Les trois articles réécrits le 16 octobre sont tous consacrés aux obligations des développeurs, et ni le moteur de recherche ni les publicités de l’App Store ne sont mentionnés dans la réforme.
Chez Google, le règlement du Play Store interdit explicitement les applis qui prétendent déshabiller les gens ou voir à travers les vêtements. Après une mise en demeure du procureur municipal de San Francisco, David Chiu, la firme de Mountain View a indiqué en juillet avoir suspendu des centaines d’applis et restreint la recherche de termes associés, dont « nudify ». David Chiu exigeait aussi d’Apple le retrait de huit applis, et l’entreprise avait alors retiré trois d’entre elles.
« Nous n’hésitons pas à retirer des applications, et à radier leurs développeurs, lorsqu’elles enfreignent ces règles », prévient Apple dans sa note. Interrogée en avril par le Tech Transparency Project sur les suggestions de son moteur de recherche, Apple n’avait pas répondu.
L’obfuscation consiste à rendre le code volontairement difficile à lire (noms de fonctions brouillés, logique éclatée, chiffrement de chaînes, etc.) afin de compliquer l’analyse. Elle peut avoir des usages légitimes (protéger une propriété intellectuelle ou limiter la rétro‑ingénierie), mais elle sert aussi à masquer des comportements interdits. Dans un processus de revue comme celui d’un magasin d’applications, l’obfuscation augmente le risque qu’une fonctionnalité réelle échappe aux vérifications. C’est particulièrement critique quand l’app peut activer à distance des modules sensibles (contenus sexuels, fraude, collecte de données) après validation. Les plateformes cherchent donc à distinguer la protection du code d’une dissimulation de fonctionnalités non déclarées.
Le “bait-and-switch” décrit le fait de soumettre une application apparemment conforme (fonctionnalités limitées, contenu neutre) pour obtenir l’approbation, puis de modifier son comportement après coup. La bascule peut se faire via une mise à jour, un paramètre caché, une configuration serveur, ou du contenu chargé dynamiquement (feature flags, modules distants). Techniquement, cela exploite le décalage entre ce qui est vérifié au moment de la soumission et ce qui est exécuté ensuite sur les appareils. Cette pratique est problématique car elle contourne les garde-fous de sécurité, de protection des mineurs et de conformité légale. Les stores tentent de la contrer en imposant la déclaration complète des fonctions et en sanctionnant les mécanismes de déclenchement dissimulés.
Le DMA (Digital Markets Act) est un règlement européen qui impose des obligations spécifiques aux grandes plateformes considérées comme “gatekeepers”, dont l’ouverture à des modes de distribution d’apps autres que le magasin officiel. Concrètement, cela peut permettre l’installation d’applications via des boutiques tierces ou des mécanismes alternatifs, tout en maintenant des exigences de sécurité et de conformité. Pour les développeurs, cela introduit plusieurs voies de diffusion, chacune avec ses propres règles, contrôles et responsabilités. Pour les plateformes, l’enjeu est d’empêcher que des apps interdites sur la boutique principale réapparaissent via ces circuits parallèles. D’où l’importance d’aligner les interdictions (exploitation, abus, contenus illégaux) sur l’ensemble des canaux, pas seulement sur le store historique.

articles.title: India’s massive AI opportunity; Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
articles.text:
India’s massive AI opportunity; Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
Unlike previous digital revolutions (internet and smartphones) that democratised access, AI is democratising intelligence itself, raising overall productivity across sectors.
Dear Reader,
The high-stakes game for India’s satellite internet is on.
Reliance Industries has officially responded to Elon Musk’s sharp critiques of India’s satellite communications landscape. Breaking its silence, the conglomerate welcomed incoming competition, saying that a competitive market ultimately serves customers best, provided every player abides by Indian law. Setting "the facts on record," Reliance directly addressed Musk's push for open competition.
Meanwhile AI company RapidCanvas has raised $29 million in Series B funding led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India. The round also saw participation from Hitachi Ventures and existing investors, including Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures.
It plans to use the capital to grow its go-to-market teams and expand its network of private equity and advisory partners, who bring managed AI execution to their portfolio companies and clients. It will also expand its field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil.
ICYMI: The grand finale of TechSparks featured Professor Ashok Jhunjhunwala, Institute Professor at IIT Madras and Chairman of IIIT Hyderabad and the ITEL Foundation, Food Pharmer Revant Himatsingka and more.
Lastly, Tesla has unveiled its next-generation Roadster in Texas, showcasing SpaceX-developed thrusters that reportedly enable the electric sports car to hover and maneuver in mid-air. Presenting the vehicle at a SpaceX facility, CEO Elon Musk teased the crowd with a preview of its wild capabilities: “You're going to see some crazy stuff tonight.”
However, it is unlikely that we will see flying cars anytime soon. Here’s why.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- India’s massive AI opportunity
- Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
Here’s your trivia for today: What consumer tech brand takes its name from the Swedish words for "electric" and "light" after a landmark merger in 1919? (Scroll down for the answer)
TechSparks
India’s massive AI opportunity
At TechSparks 2026, industry leaders Ashutosh Sharma from Prosus and Keshav Reddy from Equal AI discussed India’s rapidly growing AI landscape during a session hosted by Shradha Sharma. They emphasised that while current discussions focus on a $100 billion opportunity, AI could eventually add up to $1 trillion to India's GDP by 2035.
Unlike previous digital revolutions (internet and smartphones) that democratised access, AI is democratising intelligence itself, raising overall productivity across sectors.
Key takeaways:
- To capitalise on this shift, Indian startups must leverage local nuances to solve large, unaddressed domestic problems in areas like healthcare, education, and consumer services (such as spam call management).
- Ashutosh Sharma, Head of Investments and M&A, India, Prosus, said local understanding would be a key differentiator for Indian startups competing with international companies.
- Success lies in targeting specific, widespread local pain points. As an example, Reddy spoke about Equal AI scaling to millions of users by addressing India's severe spam call issue.
Inspiration
Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
Across India, women are transforming local skills and natural resources into thriving ventures—spanning floriculture, solar energy, and sustainable fish farming.
Featured on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Mann Ki Baat in 2026, their success stories underscore a powerful playbook for rural economic growth: combining hands-on training and institutional backing with reliable credit and direct market connections allows women entrepreneurs to build sustainable businesses.
Key takeaways:
- Sujata Bhuyan, a homemaker from Odisha’s Sambalpur district, ventured into fish farming to supplement her family’s income. Her annual fish production has increased to 25-30 metric tonnes, earning her an annual income of Rs 7–10 lakh, according to the Indian Council of Agricultural Research
- Payal Munjpara, from Surendranagar district in Gujarat, has become a solar entrepreneur. As a solar technician, Munjpara works on rooftop solar installations across neighbouring districts, earning a livelihood through her skills.
- Babita Sharma, a street vendor from Nandgram in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, turned a small roadside stall selling religious offerings into a growing business with support from the PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme.
News & updates
- Onboarding: Real estate classifieds Magicbricks has appointed Mayank Jain as chief executive officer (CEO), effective October 1. In a statement on Friday, Magicbricks, one of the leading property platforms, said Jain has joined from CarDekho, where he served for over five years as CEO of Auto Classifieds.
- In the red: Maestroedge Solutions, which runs home services platform Snabbit, has posted a net loss of Rs 167.75 crore for 2025-26, nearly 30 times lower than the previous year, as spending on service providers, marketing and staff rose with the expansion of its business.
What consumer tech brand takes its name from the Swedish words for "electric" and "light" after a landmark merger in 1919?
Answer: Electrolux

articles.title: À moins de 30 000 €, Volkswagen propose un nouveau SUV électrique avec 1 300 km d'autonomie pour redresser la barre après des ventes décevantes
articles.text:
À moins de 30 000 €, Volkswagen propose un nouveau SUV électrique avec 1 300 km d'autonomie pour redresser la barre après des ventes décevantes
Volkswagen est en train de vivre une situation très compliquée avec des licenciements de masse et la menace de fermeture d’usines. L’entreprise allemande a donc tout intérêt à redresser la barre sur le plus important des marchés des voitures électriques : la Chine.
Volkswagen est dans une situation compliquée et pour relancer ses ventes, l’entreprise allemande lance l’ID. ERA 8X, un grand SUV cinq places qui propose environ 1 300 kilomètres d’autonomie pour un tarif autour de 27 500 €. C’est donc là-bas qu’est lancé l’ID. ERA 8X, qui propose propulsion électrique et moteur essence utilisé comme générateur. Bref, un SUV premium pour le prix d’un modèle bien plus modeste en France.
Volkswagen lance son SUV ID. ERA 8X
À noter que cet ID. ERA 8X est le fruit de la coentreprise entre Volkswagen et SAIC, firme chinoise. Avec les promotions, le prix de départ est de 206 800 ¥, soit autour de 27 500 €. Les tarifs montent jusqu’à 269 800 ¥, soit environ 35 900 €. Le tarif en dehors des promotions débute à 226 800 ¥, soit environ 30 100 €.
En termes de fiche technique, l’ID. ERA 8X, c’est un SUV long de 5,02 mètres et presque 2 mètres de large pour un empattement qui atteint 2,97 mètres. Le choix de Volkswagen est tout trouvé pour ce modèle : cinq places et le confort maximum.
Dans l’habitacle, on trouve deux écrans de 15,6 pouces en définition 2,5K, un affichage tête haute, des sièges de première rangée avec massage, du cuir Nappa et un réfrigérateur de 12 litres. Sur les portes se trouvent aussi des écrans intégrés.
Sous la carrosserie, le SUV de Volkswagen repose sur un moteur essence de 1,5 litre de 143 chevaux pour générer de l’électricité. Les roues sont entraînées par un ou deux moteurs électriques selon la finition choisie. La puissance atteint jusqu’à 299 chevaux sur les versions propulsion et jusqu’à 517 chevaux avec quatre roues motrices.
La plus rapide des versions de ce SUV électrique passe de 0 à 100 km/h en 4,6 secondes. Volkswagen propose deux batteries avec 51,1 kWh mais surtout 65,2 kWh qui offre 451 kilomètres d’autonomie en mode électrique selon la norme CLTC.
Quand la batterie et le réservoir sont utilisés, l’autonomie totale officielle atteint 1 602 kilomètres selon la norme chinoise CLTC. Soit 1 300 kilomètres le cycle européen WLTC. L’architecture 800 V permet de passer de 10 à 80 % de batterie en 16 minutes.
Le SUV a aussi le droit à une aide à la conduite Momenta R7 avec un LiDAR à 192 lignes et 26 capteurs. Une technologie qui permet de gérer la conduite assistée sur autoroute, en ville et lors des manœuvres de stationnement.
Volkswagen cherche à redresser la barre
Bien évidemment, face aux constructeurs chinois très agressifs en termes de prix comme BYD ou Xpeng, l’entreprise allemande mise sur un prix accessible. Wu Yun, directeur général de la coentreprise SAIC Volkswagen, assume cette stratégie agressive face au marché chinois.
"Nous participons à la guerre des prix, mais pas au prix de pertes durables", explique le dirigeant. L’objectif est tout trouvé : reprendre des parts de marché face à BYD et Xpeng cités précédemment, ou encore Li Auto et Xiaomi qui arrive en Europe.
Volkswagen a aussi réduit le temps de développement de l’ID. ERA 8X à environ deux ans. Fabio Stoelzel, vice-président de SAIC Volkswagen Sales, explique : "Le développement peut aller plus vite, mais la validation ne peut pas être réduite."
Lors des tests, le SUV électrique a dépassé un million de kilomètres et 25 000 heures sur banc d’essai, une installation qui permet de tester les composants dans des conditions contrôlées pour mesurer leur résistance et leur fiabilité.
Malheureusement, Volkswagen n’a annoncé aucune commercialisation de l’ID. ERA 8X en Europe. Donc pour le moment, le SUV chinois de l’entreprise allemande n’est disponible que pour les consommateurs chinois.

articles.title: Una joven de 17 años creó un detector de terremotos con solo 100 dólares y funciona en Los Ángeles
articles.text:
Durante el confinamiento por la pandemia, Vivien He, una estudiante de secundaria de California, dedicó su tiempo libre a construir un sismógrafo. Con un presupuesto inferior a 100 dólares, aprendió electrónica y programación por su cuenta, soldó los componentes y diseñó el dispositivo. El resultado fue un detector sísmico compacto que logró registrar terremotos en el área de Los Ángeles.
El aparato, del tamaño aproximado de un cubo de Rubik y protegido por una carcasa transparente de acrílico, se puso a prueba muy pronto: un día después de que He terminara de montarlo, ocurrió un terremoto en Los Ángeles. La onda registrada por el dispositivo casero coincidió con la de una estación del Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS), según el relato sobre el proyecto.
El sismógrafo utiliza un geófono para captar el movimiento del suelo. Luego, la electrónica y el software convierten esa señal en una onda digital. Si el movimiento supera el umbral establecido, el sistema puede hacer sonar una alarma y enviar un mensaje de texto. También se controla desde un teléfono móvil y tiene capacidad para almacenar hasta cuatro años de registros.
Un detector económico para alertar sobre terremotos
El proyecto de He apuntó a una necesidad concreta: acercar la detección sísmica a las personas mediante un dispositivo de bajo costo. Los sistemas profesionales, como ShakeAlert, requieren una red de sensores y una infraestructura especializada. El aparato de la estudiante, en cambio, fue concebido para funcionar en una vivienda y ofrecer una opción accesible.
El sismógrafo no predice los terremotos. Los sistemas de alerta temprana tampoco pueden anticiparlos: detectan el sismo una vez que comenzó y envían avisos antes de que lleguen las ondas más destructivas a ciertos lugares.
Un terremoto genera, entre otras, ondas P y ondas S. Las primeras viajan más rápido y pueden detectarse antes; las segundas llegan después y suelen causar más daños. Esa diferencia permite ganar tiempo para tomar medidas, aunque el margen depende de la distancia al epicentro y de las condiciones del sismo.
Según el USGS, ShakeAlert puede ofrecer desde unos pocos segundos hasta decenas de segundos de aviso en la costa oeste de Estados Unidos. Cerca del epicentro, el tiempo disponible puede ser mínimo.
Cómo aprendió a construirlo
He contó a la publicación EOS, de la Unión Geofísica Estadounidense, que no tenía formación previa en electrónica ni programación. Aprendió Python por su cuenta, consultó investigaciones sobre detección de terremotos y buscó respuestas a medida que avanzaba. En sus palabras, “googleaba todo”.
La idea inicial surgió al observar cómo cambió el ruido sísmico durante los confinamientos. La actividad cotidiana —como el transporte, las fábricas y el movimiento de las personas— produce vibraciones que pueden registrarse con instrumentos sensibles. En 2020, cuando gran parte de esa actividad se detuvo, el ruido sísmico disminuyó y fue posible observar señales débiles que normalmente quedaban ocultas.
Ese contexto llevó a He a preguntarse si podía medir las vibraciones desde su propia casa. El proyecto evolucionó hasta incorporar funciones de alerta. En 2021, presentó el dispositivo en una reunión de la Sociedad Sismológica de América.
Qué pudo detectar en California
Entre septiembre de 2020 y abril de 2021, el instrumento registró los terremotos de magnitud superior a 3,0 ocurridos en los alrededores de Los Ángeles, de acuerdo con la información divulgada sobre el proyecto. Esa capacidad mostró que un equipo construido con piezas accesibles podía captar actividad sísmica real y almacenar datos útiles.
El detector de Vivien He no reemplaza las redes científicas ni ofrece garantías para anticipar cada movimiento. Su experiencia sí muestra cómo un dispositivo económico puede acercar la observación sísmica a los hogares y ayudar a comprender la actividad del suelo.
Para los residentes de Los Ángeles, donde los terremotos forman parte del riesgo cotidiano, unos segundos de alerta pueden servir para reaccionar: alejarse de ventanas, buscar un lugar seguro y prepararse para el movimiento.

articles.title: DroidDeck convierte tu móvil Android en una Steam Deck para jugar a juegos de PC en local y sin streaming: así funciona
articles.text:
Prácticamente todo el mundo tiene un móvil en su bolsillo. Y durante años, muchas compañías de videojuegos, estudios de desarrollo y editoras han querido convertirlo además en una máquina para jugar. El juego en móvil ha evolucionado tremendamente desde sus inicios, pero siempre he tenido la espinita clavada de poder jugar a mis juegos de PC desde el móvil.
El streaming satisface esa necesidad, pero a pesar de que ya encontramos sistemas que funcionan francamente bien y muy estables, como es el caso de GeForce NOW para el juego en la nube, o Apollo streaming + el cliente de Moonlight para jugar a los juegos de tu PC, al final siempre vas a depender de una conexión a internet.
Bueno, pues lo de jugar a tus juegos de PC desde el móvil y completamente en local ya es una realidad, y el proyecto de DroidDeck nace precisamente con esa intención. Te contamos cómo funciona y cómo puedes hacer funcionar tus juegos de Steam desde un móvil Android.
Qué es. DroidDeck se instala como cualquier otra aplicación de Android, pero en su interior ejecuta la versión para ARM de Steam en el modo Big Picture, ofreciendo una experiencia muy similar a la Steam Deck. Inicias sesión con tu cuenta de Steam, accedes a tu biblioteca y descargas los juegos directamente al teléfono.
La app también incluye compatibilidad con Steam Input para jugar con cualquier mando, opciones de superposición para trazara el rendimiento de los juegos, gestión de los drivers de tu GPU y hasta opciones de generación de fotogramas. Junto a todo ello, la app también es compatible con un modo de escritorio, y hasta puedes instalar apps de Linux a través de Flatpak y AppImage. Es básicamente como tener SteamOS pero sin tener que cambiar el sistema operativo de tu móvil, y todo desde una app.
Qué tiene de especial. Ya existían otras apps que ejecutan juegos de PC localmente en Android, como GameNative, Winlator o GameHub. La diferencia de DroidDeck es que ofrece el cliente y la interfaz propios de Valve en lugar de un launcher personalizado. Y esto mola bastante, sobre todo si Steam es tu plataforma principal y disfrutas de su ecosistema.
Cómo funciona. Los juegos de Windows se ejecutan a través de Proton, la capa de compatibilidad de Valve, mientras que una capa de traducción llamada FEX convierte el código x86, para el que están creados los juegos de PC, en instrucciones que los procesadores ARM entienden. El proyecto de hecho parte de lo que Valve consiguió con sus gafas de realidad virtual Steam Frame, unas gafas con chip de móvil que ejecutan juegos de PC sin estar conectadas a uno. Este es el mismo enfoque pero orientado a teléfonos móviles. Así que ahora sí podríamos decir que merece la pena tener un móvil gaming.
Rendimiento. Lo más interesante de todo es que las cifras no están nada mal para ser un proyecto que acaba de echar a andar. ETA PRIME, creador de contenido en YouTube, ha probado la app en su Redmagic 11 Pro, móvil con chip Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 y 16 GB de RAM. Todos los juegos se ejecutaron a 720p:
- Cyberpunk 2077: alrededor de 60 fps en configuración media.
- Skyrim Special Edition: alrededor de 60 fps en configuración media.
- Left 4 Dead 2: 120 fps estables en configuración alta.
- Hogwarts Legacy: alrededor de 48 fps en configuración media, subiendo por encima de 60 fps con la generación de fotogramas FSR integrada activada.
Requisitos. DroidDeck requiere Android 9 o superior. También necesitas una chip con GPU Adreno 730 o superior, que es precisamente la GPU incorporada en los chips de Qualcomm. De momento, si tienes GPU Mali, Xclipse, PowerVR o Adreno 710 en tu teléfono, no podrás jugar. En la práctica, esto significa chips Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 en adelante. Cuando tengas la app, tendrás que instalar Linux, que ocupa unos 3 GB, y más de 1 GB adicional si quieres el entorno de escritorio y los emuladores.
Aquí el hardware de tu teléfono será especialmente importante, ya que determinará cómo de bien tirará el juego. ETA Prime añade que estos chips se sobrecalientan rápidamente al ejecutar juegos x86, y recomienda deshabilitar uno o dos núcleos de CPU para mantener el rendimiento estable con el tiempo.
Cómo instalar DroidDeck. La instalación es sencilla. Tienes que descargar el APK desde la página de GitHub del proyecto (habilitando la instalación de apps desde orígenes desconocidos). También se requiere habilitar las opciones de desarrollo y desactivar las restricciones de procesos secundarios de Android (Android’s child-process) para que Steam pueda ejecutarse. Esto se puede encontrar en el mismo menú de las opciones de desarrollador de Android.
Lo malo es que si tienes Android 13 o inferior, puede que no encuentres esa opción, así que tendrás que tirar de comandos ADB para deshabilitarla.
Y ahora qué. DroidDeck todavía se encuentra en pañales, pero es uno de los muchos proyectos que ya circulan por internet y que facilitan la instalación de juegos de PC en móviles compatibles. Esto acaba de comenzar, y todo indica a que cuando madure aún más la compatibilidad entre juegos y arquitectura arm, poco a poco veremos cómo los móviles se convertirán, esta vez de verdad, en consolas portátiles que lo ejecutan todo.

articles.title: Intel "Razor Lake-AX" to Pack 700 TOPS of AI Compute
articles.text:
Saturday, October 17th 2026
Intel "Razor Lake-AX" to Pack 700 TOPS of AI Compute
Intel's senior vice president, Cho Min-sung, announced at the Semiconductors Powering Humanoids summit in South Korea that the next-generation "Razor Lake-AX" platform will be a computing powerhouse, featuring 700 TOPS of AI compute on die. This means that at INT8/FP8 precision, "Razor Lake-AX" will outperform the current "Panther Lake" mobile chips by 3.88 times, which have a total compute power of 180 TOPS. This represents a significant boost in compute power for the SoC, primarily derived from a large integrated GPU alongside a substantial CPU complex. Earlier reports indicated that the "Razor Lake-AX" iGPU will be available in two versions: one with a 16-core iGPU and a flagship SKU with a 32-core iGPU.
Both of these integrated graphics solutions are expected to be based on Intel's Xe3 graphics IP, currently found in "Panther Lake." This would make "Razor Lake-AX" nearly three times as powerful as the current Arc B390, which powers Intel's PTL lineup. This suggests that "Razor Lake-AX" will be a large package, as the GPU die is reportedly around 162.84 mm². We also learned that Intel plans to reintroduce on-package memory with the upcoming "AX" chip. Although the company initially stated that the Core Ultra 200V "Lunar Lake" was the last design with on-package memory, Intel is reportedly bringing back on-package LPDDR5X/LPDDR6 memory for "Razor Lake-AX." Do note that the image below is simply an illustration.Additionally, it's unclear where Intel will manufacture this massive chip, but the large iGPU suggests a design powered by EMIB and Foveros 3D to interconnect various elements. Finally, the chip is expected to feature a BGA-4326 package with 4,326 pins, similar to what Intel's Xeon CPUs typically use. Previously, Intel was considering a "Nova Lake-AX" SoC featuring 48 Xe3 cores paired with a 28-core CPU cluster. However, this has been put on hold, and the "AX" generation will not debut with the upcoming "Nova Lake" generation. Intel plans to launch the first batch of chips with the "AX" suffix after "Nova Lake," with "Razor Lake-AX" expected to arrive in 2028.

articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Rivian's next act | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!
As I wrapped my TechCrunch Disrupt interview with Rivian CEO and founder RJ Scaringe, I kept circling back to one question: What does Scaringe want Rivian to become? If you look at Rivian’s moves over the past year, it’s clear that Scaringe wants the company to be much more than an EV maker. But he doesn’t want to stray completely from that mission either.
Rivian is far more vertically integrated than it was just a couple of years ago. It has developed its own AI models to power its in-vehicle assistant and is building an end-to-end automated driving stack for its passenger vehicles and future robotaxis through a partnership with Uber. It’s even developing custom silicon, a 5 nm processor in collaboration with Arm and TSMC. And then there is its $5.8 billion joint technology venture with VW Group focused on electric architecture and software.
Scaringe’s ambitions extend beyond Rivian as well, although there is always a link back. He created a micromobility skunkworks program that has since spun out into a startup called Also. And he founded an industrial robotics startup called Mind Robotics, which is now 31% owned by Rivian and counts the automaker as a prospective customer. (Scaringe announced onstage that former Ford, Apple, and Tesla executive Doug Field has been hired as president of Mind Robotics.)
Scaringe’s aspirations were on display as he talked of not only expanding the joint venture with VW to cover AI and autonomy, but also licensing Rivian’s tech to “many different brands.”
So what does Rivian look like at the end of the decade? Certainly not just a maker of electric trucks and SUVs. The term I kept coming back to was “tech supplier.”
Hear me out. Rivian is clearing a path toward licensing its electric architecture and software as well as its AI models and autonomy stack. Meanwhile, the Mind Robotics startup it partially owns is building industrial robots to not only be used in Rivian factories, but also sold to other companies. Then there’s the robotaxi business. A successful launch with Uber could open the door to more deals.
And Scaringe is already imagining how autonomy could reshape Rivian’s own vehicles.
“Where it gets really interesting is then you think beyond R2 and R3 and start to imagine the form factors that you want to build for a personally owned autonomous vehicle. You know, it opens up all kinds of design opportunities. It can create dramatically different experiences,” he said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I’m wildly excited about what the next 10 years look like in transportation because of what this enables us to dream and think about.”
Deals!
Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing autonomous driving tech for construction vehicles, is raising $600 million, Axios reported, citing sources.
Dot Ai completed its acquisition of electric vehicle car-sharing business Envoy Technologies in a $65 million all-stock transaction, according to a regulatory filing.
Evos, a startup that developed AI agents to automate work for industrial businesses, including freight brokerages, raised $9 million in a pre-seed round co-led by Uncork Capital and Field Ventures.
Mana Battery, a Colorado-based startup developing anode-free sodium batteries, raised $10.15 million in a round led by Voyager Ventures.
PlusAI, the autonomous trucking developer, and Texas Ventures Acquisition III filed a Form S-4 registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission —advancing its previously announced agreement to go public via a merger with a blank-check company.
Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia. Neither company shared financial terms of the deal. The automaker plans to use a trio of Nvidia products to be able to offer hands-free, point-to-point driving on highways and surface streets.
Waabi, a startup developing self-driving trucks, landed a commercial partnership with carrier Warrior Logistics. Under the deal, Waabi’s self-driving trucks will move freight between Dallas and Houston.
Notable reads and other tidbits
Electric vehicle sales in the United States are showing signs of life.
Laplace Intelligence, one of 20 startups that competed in TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200, is building automated red-teaming that stress-tests robots and self-driving cars.
MIT startup LNK Energies says it has created a way to convert existing heavy-duty trucks from diesel to hydrogen, slashing pollution and costs while shielding operators from price spikes.
The Paris Auto Show puts Chinese cars on center stage.
Tesla showcased its SpaceX-powered Roadster with a theatrical kickflip stunt. The Roadster used a mix of high-powered fans and thrusters to drive up an inverted ramp, spin around, and stick a landing on the pavement below. CEO Elon Musk claims the vehicle will be on the road by 2028. But will future owners be allowed to legally deploy these maneuvers on public streets? I don’t see how.
Waymo is expanding into Canada — specifically, Toronto — after receiving approval to participate in an automated vehicle pilot program. Waymo has also opened up its robotaxi service to everyone, meaning no more waitlists, in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa.
One more thing …
TechCrunch reporter Tim De Chant recently test drove the 2026Porsche Macan Turbo EV. His week with the EV has him questioning what a sports car is supposed to be. Read the full review.

articles.title: Britain's £4 billion nuclear submarines have a bizarre last line of defence
articles.text:
The UK Navy wants to use this cheap, eco-friendly system against drones — high-pressure fire hoses chosen to protect nuclear submarine fleet as 'last line of defence'
Royal Navy sailors trained to fight off drones using water jets
- Britain's nuclear submarine crews are training to fight drones using water
- Fire hoses provide emergency protection when drones breach naval security
- Each Vanguard submarine costs approximately £4 billion despite its basic defences
British sailors are receiving training to repel hostile drones using powerful water jets aboard nuclear submarines stationed at a naval installation in Scotland.
The unconventional approach provides a relatively inexpensive and environmentally friendly defensive option for vessels facing potential aerial attacks while docked or operating above water.
A report from The Sun, the equipment serves as an emergency measure when incoming drones penetrate existing security arrangements around Britain's nuclear deterrent.
High-pressure water jets provide final protection
The Royal Navy has equipped its Vanguard-class submarines with firefighting hoses capable of directing concentrated streams of water toward approaching unmanned aircraft.
These devices feature handheld nozzles with pistol-style controls, allowing sailors to aim pressurised water at airborne threats approaching their vessels.
During an attack, sailors would direct powerful water jets at small and medium-sized FPV drones, attempting to knock them down or divert their flight paths.
The hoses are deployed aboard submarines stationed at HMNB Clyde; the Scottish naval installation responsible for accommodating Britain's nuclear deterrent fleet.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Unlike conventional air defence systems, the hoses cannot detect or automatically track incoming drones.
A naval source acknowledged the limitations of relying on firefighting equipment against airborne threats.
But when in a dire situation, “you have to use what you’ve got,” said an unnamed Royal Navy source.
The Vanguard-class vessels reportedly cost approximately £4 billion each, making their reliance on water-based protection particularly striking.
These submarines carry Trident II D5 ballistic missiles equipped with nuclear warheads, forming the maritime component of Britain's strategic deterrence capability.
Although the hoses provide no conventional anti-aircraft weaponry, they offer crews an immediate means of responding when other defensive measures fail.
Their practical value will depend on whether sailors can deploy them quickly enough against threats that evade existing defences.
Naval base faces potential close-range drone attacks
This arrangement addresses particular vulnerabilities where submarines become more exposed to aerial surveillance and attacks during port operations.
HMNB Clyde occupies a location beside Gare Loch, a relatively confined Scottish waterway measuring approximately one kilometre across at certain points.
Nearby hills, accessible roads and surrounding terrain could allow hostile operators to launch drones without providing defenders sufficient warning.
Such geographical constraints create additional security challenges because relatively short flight distances can significantly reduce the time available for interception.
The Ministry of Defence says military installations rely on several protective measures, including physical barriers, security patrols, surveillance equipment and counter-drone systems.
Officials have also announced £470 million in additional expenditure over four years to improve security across Britain's military facilities and installations.
These security investments become more important as underwater sensors were discovered near routes used by British submarines departing their Scottish naval headquarters.
Those devices were suspected of having possible connections to Russian efforts to monitor submarine movements, although their precise origins remain unconfirmed.

articles.title: MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke review: Taking flight sim immersion to the next level
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke Bundle delivers an incredible flight sim experience, combining force feedback, exceptional build quality, and precise control. However, the elevator can feel somewhat “sticky” without the proper settings and its premium price makes it a significant investment.
Reasons to buy
- + High level of precision
- + Exceptional build quality
- + Force feedback
- + Autopilot following
Reasons to avoid
- - Sticky along the elevator axis without the proper settings
- - Pricing
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Over the past several years, MOZA Racing has become one of the most recognizable names in sim racing, earning a reputation for producing high-quality racing wheels and peripherals. Founded in 2012 by a group of automotive engineers and sim racing enthusiasts, the company initially focused on manufacturing and selling videography equipment before entering the sim-racing market.
More recently, MOZA has expanded into the world of flight simulation, bringing the same focus on build quality and performance that has made its racing products so popular. Today, we’re taking a look at the MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke. We’ll be putting both products through their paces in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, testing them across a variety of challenging flight scenarios to see how they perform in the cockpit.

While you can purchase the base and the yoke separately, they also come in a bundle. With the bundle, you get both the yoke and the base in the box, along with a toolkit and user manual. The base comes with a power cable and a USB Type A to Type B cable.
MOZA also sent us a couple of table clamps for the yoke to secure it to our test setup. The clamps are sold separately.
